This is a hard game to reccomend so I'll just break it down pro and con wise.
PROS:
-Extremely tight and fun gameplay, controls like a wet dream
-Dual weilding whatever weapons you want makes for some great combos that make the situations and set pieces exhilerating and unique
-Visceral feedback from takedowns and kills that are immensly satisfying
-Straight up superpowers that enhance gameplay (more on that in the cons)
-Amazing soundtrack (except for one thing but again, in the cons)
-Sound design is top notch with a Shotgun and Heavy Weapons that sound meaty and like they're really meant for tearing up Nazis
-Some of the weapons are awesome. Keyword: Some
-Cinematics are well made and the voice acting is fantastic
-Overall world design is distinct and nice on the eyes
-This game is stunningly beutiful. It may not have the best textures or models. But sweet man god damn the way everything just meshes and the effects and the lighting and overal quality just leaves you jaw on the ground
CONS:
-The story sucks, just straight up sucks. The New Order was a surprising character study on BJ that made him feel almost too real. It was shocking and brutal yet poignant and hopeful. It's sci fi elements and overall silliness of the whole premise never got in the way. The set pieces felt natural to the level design and actually impacted the characters. Bombate and Klaus and Co. had purpose and felt like they gave purpose to BJ and the story. But this one is just jarringly bad. It's a revenge tale I think. I'm not sure. It feels like it tries to repeat the same steps as the New Order (You went to the Moon in NO, In NC you go to Venus! In NO you rode a mech and now in NC you'll ride a Mech DOG! etc.) but with no real impact. It shines when BJ has his inner monologues about Caroline and how he's not sure if he's truly alive yet those are limited to the first half and ultimately go nowhere. Then it cuts to these childhood flashbacks that are so silly in trying to make you believe in how racist his dad was. The only payoff being a setpiece in a courtroom and BJ reflecting on the relationship with his mother. But then it's gone and never mentioned. Infact, character arcs just seem to go nowhere. Even the Nazi's are laughably bland bad guys. Anyone with a sense of history knowledge will be taken aback by how Machine Games has hyped up the Nazis to be all encompassing moustache twirling evil. Did the Nazis hate commies and gays and jews etc. to the point of concentration camps and genocide? Yes, but suddenly they're also Slave Trade loving Atheists who just kill opposing forces and don't have conscript armies? Come on....have some consistency with history like NO had. Characters start somewhere, there's establishment, but then they're just over with no real perceivable end. Characters come and go with no real impact. Grace just takes over with little introduction meanwhile her and Horton politically soapbox a lot that feels like an actual statement by the devs to you the player instead of the characters speaking in context of the story. Overall every new character is just hamfisted in like we're inherently supposed to like them. Meanwhile, all the OG characters are just gone except for a little from Wyatt and Fergus which ultimately go nowhere. The silliness gets in the way of the plot. You'll have these little moments between Anya and BJ or Bombate and Max that get interrupted by poop jokes that are just tasteless. The pacing is all over the place. The ending is abrupt and not satisfying at all. This is a story focused game. And it's just bad.
-Length: this game is short. I took my time on Do or Die and theres really no secrets to find. There's no fun little corridors to explore with payoffs. I deliberately went slow and focused on upgrading my perks and I don't feel like the 14 hours I took were worth it. Not to mention the ending just comes out of nowhere. In NO you knew you were coming up on the final mission, you were pumped, you were psyched. In this, it just shows up. The story starts to slowly gain traction and you feel like maybe you're a few missions away and then BAM! It's over.
-That ending song. That ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ized version of Twisted Sisters "We're Not Gonna Take It" made only to fit Mick Gordon's dark and melodic soundtrack (which is fantastic) is so out of place as with the ending.
-You get superpowers, and only one of them is actually usefull. You get a suit from the beginning that cripples you, then you get rid of it and choose from 3 mechanized super enhancements that ultimately do not benefit you at all except for deliberate level design. Only one of them enhances the gameplay and that's the Ramshackles. The Stilts and Harness have no place in the gameplay world. The Stilts conflict with the run n' gun style gameplay and the harness is only usefull for maybe a handful of stealth areas and grabbing secrets. Other than that, totally worthless. Maybe if there was more time to flesh them out (I.E. You can quick slide into small openings and quickly crawl away to break line of sight for a more predator stealth. The stilts allowed specific takedowns on certain enemies etc.) they'd be fine. But until then, Ramshackles. Oh and the stomp is pointless outside of one mission.
-Timeline specific weapons are pointless as well except for Fergus' as it helps with robot enemies
-There's little creativity to the weapons. The shotgun is fine as is the handgun and the little hand held rocket launcher. But there's no space rifle, the SMG is useless even when fully upgraded (it's suppressor is pointless for stealth), the Assault Rifle just becomes an armor piercing mini machine gun (no rocket launcher attachment) with DMR properties. They feel bland and limiting.
-The stealth is almost binary. That's all that needs to be said.
So in the end I'd still reccomend it but that comes with some stipulation. Don't buy it for its story alone, buy it if you enjoy Machine Games' gameplay design and can tolerate the terrible story. Or wait for a sale. Or just don't get it at all. Your choice. Is it a 9/10 GOAT? No. It's not. It's maybe a hard 7.5. That's not bad. But don't let games journos fool you into thinking it's anything but passable.

Okay, overall, I thought this game had a good concept, okay execution, and pretty good voice acting.
If you're looking for a game with a beautiful word, you'll find it in the city of Neo-Paris. But what disappointed me upon first play was that the world was not as interactive as I thought it would be, considering how much detail went into interesting rooms and objects that you merely passed by during gameplay. Like the robots that scatter around the city of Neo-Paris. I wish they served more of a purpose within the game because they're everywhere, but they're not mentioned at all in the storyline.
To be honest, everything about this game felt like a half-full & half-empty glass of milk. After the first major secret of Nilin's past was revealed, most of the rest of the game became predictable. I liked Nilin as the main protagonist, but I believe that a lot of the side characters just lacked reason for their actions, or they just... weren't very convincing as villains or stricken heroes. The reasons didn't convince me and felt forced. And also, I felt like the game was trying to do TOO much. There were too many things that the game wanted to include in the story and that's where all the stuff fell flat because it got boring after awhile, and the story seemed overstretched. Instead of episodes and quantity in information, they should've gone with quality and precise information. The explanation of some back characters also weren't very clear, and a lot of characters who were important in one episode were forgotten for the rest of the game or came back at awkward or weird parts of the story. The messy use of the side characters kinda made me confused and bored as well because frankly, after that character was gone so long, I had stopped caring about them and any character deaths weren't very sad for me. And the emotions and relationships felt fake since we only saw that character once or twice before so there was not really much of a connection that had me emotionally invested in the game.
Anyway, that's just some of the bad things that I had to get off my chest. Regarding the good things, like I said, the world is very beautiful. The first major plot twist was very interesting (though the rest proved predictable afterwards). Nilin was excellent as a main protagonist suffering from amnesia, and I thought that was very clever because we, as the players, could learn along in the game as she did. The mechanics of the memory remixes were very fun because I made♥♥♥♥♥♥go wrong just for the heck of it, and I wish they included more options for the memory remixes to create more outcomes. Either way, I really liked the whole "memory hunter/remixer" thing going on. Another thing I really liked was the parkour stuff, climbing walls and scaling odd structures. Wish they could've also incorporated more of that actually...
Anyway, I'm really in-between in the game. I think it's a good game to play once, but even then, I don't think it's a very memorable game other than its interesting concept and pretty art. I'd recommend getting it on a sale if possible.

This was one of those games that was on my wishlist for almost a year before I finally bought it. It was one of those games that appealed to me, but I didn't think it'd be very special so I never went ahead and bought it. A few months ago I picked it up in a sale and I'm SO glad I did. Although not flawless, it's an amazing game. The story is very touching and the graphics are beautiful. The soundtrack is great too - it puts it all together and it matches the atmosphere perfectly. The game is difficult, but most of the time not frustratingly so - although there's a few difficulty spikes that got me mashing alt-f4. Overcoming these difficulty spikes is very satisfying.
Pros:
-Stunning graphics
-Great soundtrack
-Touching story
-Controls feel very smooth and intuitive (xbox 360 wired controller)
-Combat is simple yet fun and engaging
-Lots of secrets to find; It's fun to use newly obtained skills to further explore old zones and reach places you couldn't reach before
-One big world makes the game feel less linear/more explorable, yet it's still always clear where to go
-There doesn't seem to be 'one way to go' when it comes to spending your XP points, which I like; Everything seems to be viable and a lot comes down to personal choice rather than having to follow a build in order to be able to enjoy the game
Cons:
-Some enemies are overused; As the game progresses you'll just meet more advanced types of the same enemies in some cases
-The difficulty curve isn't very consistent; Difficulty spikes occasionally make for a frustrating experience
-Not all cutscenes can be skipped (not that I've ever wanted to in this game)
-Some zones can't be revisited, making some rewards unavailable after finishing the zone

You should definitely get this, if you like metroidvania-style games. It's more about platforming than shooting, as most enemies can be killed by spamming the attack button a few times, no targeting necessary. It's not an easy game, though. There are a few sections where your platforming skills are put to the test. Instead of boss battles, there are sections where you have to avoid all obstacles while moving forward as fast as you can. These are the hardest levels of the game, where you will die many many times (and also swear a lot!).
The presentation is excellent with gorgeous graphics and natural animation. The soundtrack is also very good, with relaxing and intense tunes, depending on what's going on on the screen. The story is simple, but memorable. Be prepared to shed a tear or two.

Also feel like
theme was repeated too many times. Otherwise it was just ambient music that added little to the music. The soundtrack is ok, but overrated IMO
You really only get around half of the upgrades, which removes a big part of the gameplay. You kind of have to look through every crack and corner to find the energy stuff to upgrade them, and more often than not you have to backtrack, BUT THERE IS NO FAST TRAVEL IN ANY WAY (the definitive edition have this, but it's just the same game with added stuff. Basically a finished version of the original game). This really draws you out of the atmosphere if you want all of the content.
This leads me onto my next point. This game didn't find a good balance between gameplay and atmosphere. It feels like one team worked on each thing, and didn't really work together. It's hard to explain, but it just felt... weird. It might just be me being picky. One of the highlights of the game gameplay-wise was jumping around with the dash ability, dodging attacks and re-directing them. Sadly, this game too late into the game, and it's the only fun upgrade. The others are climbing vertically and using a strong AoE attack which you will never use, amongst other abilities you only have to use to advance in the game. In other words, there are few you'll actually use other than to complete the game.
IMO, the only positive thing this game has is the atmosphere, but even that's not enough for some people.
I would recommend metroid games if you want to play a metroidvania. Would buy this only if it was on sale.

Stop what you’re doing, do yourself a favour, just go buy and play this game. Or wait for a discount, it’s your wallet after all. I mean who am I to tell you how to live your life. I heard that they give you discounts up to 70%, which is always great. But this game is worth to buy either way.
The Incredible Adventures of Van Helsing, to which I’ll be referring as “TIAoVH” from now on for convenience purposes, is a great game with it’s gothic/steampunk atmosphere and memorable characters. The game takes place in the 19th-century Eastern Europe where magic and weird technology is real. You play as the son of the famous vampire hunter Abraham Van Helsing and take on various adventures in order to defeat the reign of the mad scientists Dr. Fulmigati. Of course you encounter a wide variety of enemies from robots to werewolfs, harpies to mutant abominations, bandits to creatures that'll be the very seed of your nightmares on the way. I mean, come on, it wouldn’t be a Van Helsing game unless you get to kill tons of different mobs. Also, your lovely ghost companion Lady Katarina is there to help you out along your journey. The balance between the characteristics of charming and witty Katarina and more down to earth, serious Helsing makes the dialogue in game much more enjoyable.
In TIAoVH you can use both melee and ranged weapons and make them viable on one character depending on your build. There are also other passive and active supporting skills for both Lady Katarina and Van Helsing. You can also switch Lady Katarina between melee, ranged and ghost modes. You can send her back to sell items when your inventory is full. Just like a Torchlight pet, but more useful most of the time. Also if you buy the DLC’s you get access to two more classes, Thaumaturge, a mage-like class and Arcane Mechanic, an engineer type class. All three classes have different skill trees and gameplay mechanics. The skill point reset system had some bugs that made changing builds a living hell, but the lovely developers implemented bugfix chat codes so they shouldn’t bother the player anymore.
In some other reviews, I came across people comparing TIAoVH to other, similar games. Although I think it is completely natural to do so, there are couple of things they are missing. While comparing games the gameplay shouldn’t be the only aspect. The price tag, release date, the theme etc. should also be taken in consideration. And I’d say all things considered TIAoVH is one of the best games on the Isometric RPG market.
Now, of course TIAoVH too has it’s cons. Personally, I love most of the achievements in this game. They provide you with some challenging gameplay and replayability. And while I am a big fan of challenging achievements, I can’t say I enjoy grindy achievements one bit. Not killing a single type of enemy throughout the game for an achievement, fun. Killing 500000 monsters to complete an achievement, not fun. But in the end earning achievements is up to the player. Some people might just say meh, while others like yours truly may spend over a hundred hours playing, chasing monsters left and right. Well, I think it was still worth it.
There are times playing co-op feels almost impossible with constant bugs and crashes. The worst part is, it completely depends on your luck. Sometimes me and my friends play for hours with no problems. But sometimes we crash so much that we eventually stop playing. I mean, it is still manageable. But if you’re buying this game to play with friends you better strengthen your nerves.
Another downside of the game, to me personally, was the ending. They left it on such a cliffhanger that made it feel almost incomplete. But considering that there are three more TIAoVH games out there makes it a bit easier to deal with.
All and all, I’d say this game is definitely worth your dime. It has great visuals and a good story. You can always spice things up with different challenges. And the game keeps you entertained with it’s perfectly timed pop culture references throughout the gameplay.

Wolfenstein: The New Order was a major surprise in 2014. I assumed it wouldn't be any good and was plesantly surprised by how great it was. The New Colosus had some big shoes to fill and I think it has done a spectacular job of living up to that legacy. Like the first game, the writing is top notch. The story and characters are as great as ever. Shooting is smooth and fun. Graphics are pretty great, though some character models look dated. Stealth is good in places but can often be obtuse and every segment relies too heavily on killing officers. Weapons are great if lacking in variety and the perk system from the first game is greatly improved to facility a play style that makes sense. Generally the New Colosus is a major improvement over the New Order and I highly recommend it. It's a solid 10 hour campaign with some fun bonus missions after the main story and DLC to come. If you're like me and enjoy a good single player shooter with a narrative focus you can't go wrong with Wolfenstein.

From the six hours I've played, I'd actually say I've enjoyed the story, gunplay, and presentation of The New Colossus. If you're a fan of The New Order and The Old Blood, then this won't disappoint on that front. However, I would strongly recommend that you don't pick this game up at present. The game has a variety of technical issues (I experienced some frustrating crashing myself that I fixed by trying a number of random fixes, installing new drivers, and rebooting a bunch) that make it somewhat difficult to recommend at present.
The biggest issue that I am aware of, and that effected me personally, is that patches will reset your progress in ongoing levels. I had put quite a bit of time into a level, downloaded the update, and then found out that I'd have to replay the whole thing. This is ludicrous and quite frustrating. No thanks. I'll probably change my review to a recommended after they stop updating the game and adding DLC, but for the time being, leave it alone.

I lost interest in The New Order and The Old Blood about halfway through each, but this one I played all the way through and I love it. The New Colossus has many flaws, but it's hard not to be charmed by its over-the-top weirdness. There's so many moments that I can honestly say I've never seen in a game before.
The combat is fast and brutal. You can find hidden weapon upgrades that slightly increase your power throughout the game, but for the most part it's a standard weapon set. You can also scavenge for big guns that use wall chargers. Stealth is very difficult, but it's satisfying just to take down a few guards before the alarms go off. The environments all look great, but I found myself getting lost fairly often and getting stuck on invisible walls.
The cast of characters have frustrating quirks, but these often play out to great affect when they clash or cooperate. Not all the jokes land, but there's some genuinely hilarious moments. The cut scene editing is excellent and keeps the story moving at a perfect pace. And then there's a moment in the middle that I won't spoil which is one of the single greatest twists I've ever seen in a game. My jaw dropped and it still makes me laugh when I think about it.
There's tones of secrets in the game: diaries, concept art, cards, etc. I didn't find any of this compelling because I mostly mashed the pick-up button while sprinting through environments. But they have a nice in-fiction system for returning to previous levels and collectors can significantly extend the game's lifetime.
The run and gun aspects are a little repetitive by the end, and the conclusion is very abrupt and unsatisfying, but I was toughly entertained despite its stumbles.

I'll start with the cons: Several people complained about achievements not popping up in windows 10, so before I started playing at my own risk, I decided to follow a community guide to a "safe" mode to avoid complications. Specially the "windowed mode" part, which I know can be a deal breaker for some.
Getting past that, the game itself is great, the puzzles are usually fluid and very logical (when compared to many other games), the story is engaging and never felt boring (at least for me). I still got stuck a couple times, but during most of the gameplay, finding your next action is straight-forward and yet it still feels rewarding when you "make the story go forward". Being able to go back and forth between the 2 characters is a nice feature and the change of atmosphere contributes to keeping things fresh. There is even a (not very deep) "decisions matter" system and a small branch of choices at the end. Recommended.

1954 Alcatraz is a pretty alright adventure game, as far as adventure games made past the 90's and early 00's go. The story is that you control either Joe or Christine and try to find a way for Joe to get off the island and Christine to not end up at the bottom of the bay as a result of her criminal connections.
The era, dialogue, and characters are all interesting and well worth the price of admission for the game, but that's about all there is. The gameplay is very limited, much like the simplicity of Telltale titles but without anything being totally obvious. Aside from a few select choices, there's very little variation in the story. None of the puzzles are too perplexing, and work within realistic physics so no worry of chicken-pulleys here.
Though, buyer beware, this game is not unlike Telltale titles in that it's buggy. I had one progress blocker where my character was stuck in a position unable to take any actions, and because it was a pseudo cutscene I couldn't pause to restart. Mind, this wasn't a crash, my character was still doing his breathing animation and the sounds were as though nothing had changed. In addition, there's a pretty widespread problem where the Steam achievements don't work, and the developer is delightfully ignoring this glaring, consistent, issue. There also doesn't seem like there'll be any patch to fix it, as I've had this title for about a year and so far nothing.
In summary: The game would be good, worth about 5 bucks at the most, but only if a patch comes out that fixes most of the foreseeable bugs. Until then, this is a story you can ignore.

The Good: Amazing story, beautifully created visually and technically, lots of different missions to complete, parkour and crowd system are unique and revolutionary, DirectX 10 looks great
The Bad: Some control and clipping issues, extremely repetitive missions, not very diverse visually, crowd simulation gets predictable and repetitive
Nothing is true. Everything is permitted. This is a saying heard throughout Assassin's Creed and it really sticks with you. So does the thick plot that has come to take the game industry by storm as well as one of the greatest game characters of all time: Altair. The plot is actually weird at first because it's a sci-fi story. You are actually Desmond Miles capture by modern world Templars. They stick you in an Animus and use your DNA to access your ancestors memories to find the Piece of Eden which can be used to control people's minds. That one ancestor is Altair set during the crusades. The second story is of Altair who ends up losing his rank and status among the Assassin Brotherhood by failing a mission due to eagerness and stupidity. Your master, Al Mualim, sends on special missions to assassinate key leaders throughout the holy land (Acre, Jerusalem, and Damascus) to keep them from taking the Piece of Eden and using it to win the war.
As you can see the plot is very interesting with a lot of twists. How is the game though? You have a huge open world that are full of side missions and hundreds of buildings to climb. Assassin's Creed has a parkour climbing system as well as a puppeteering system. You control each of Altair's limbs in two different states. The "socially acceptable" state allows you to use eagle vision which can show enemies and key targets. You can gently push people away from you and this is key because is you're running around the city knocking people over the guards will come after you, and towards the end of the game everyone is highly suspicious of you and just a few people knocked over will have the entire guard on your tail. The third thing is obviously combat, but if you hold down the run button you start climbing buildings, grabbing people to toss them, and jumping around.
Assassin's Creed really tried to introduce crowd psychology into the game and it works here, but does feel limited. If you climb buildings people will react by stopping and staring and saying things accordingly. If you use ladders people don't mind so much. While using rooftops is faster and keeps you away from most guards you must watch out for guards on rooftops who will shoot you with arrows if you don't get down, kill them, or move away quickly. The climbing works well enough, but there are some controls issues, clipping issues, and other issues with the camera. When Altair is facing a different way then the camera he will jump towards his way instead of the way you're telling him too. Also, if you run around a pole or near a crate he'll start climbing it instead of just jumping over or going around. This can get down right frustrating when you are running away from a dozen guards and trying to find a hiding spot.
The game also introduces anonymity via a symbol near your health bar which stays white when no ones suspects you, but will turn yellow when you are watched and flash red when guards are on to you. When it does this get away quickly or kill whomever is watching you. Don't just kill out in the open or people will run around screaming and call guards. Get away from dead bodies quickly because guards will come by and try to find who killed them or citizens will give you away. If you are caught you need to kill all guards after you or hide. To do this you must break their line of sight and the symbol will flash yellow. When it does find a hiding spot quickly before it turns red again. You can hide on benches between people, stacks of hay, in groups of monks praying, or draped boxes on rooftops. Stay there for a few seconds and you will by anonymous again. You can avoid all this chaos by just jogging, staying calm, don't flail around and jump around like a monkey in crowded areas etc.
This whole crowd system is really something else and works well, but feels repetitive and predictable because of the recycled sayings, animations, and it always happens the same way. The combat is the same way because while you can gain new abilities it feels like a counter fest. You can attack with a sword or short sword, throw daggers, but most guards always block and you just stand there with the block button held down and wait for someone to attack and then counter which is usually an instant kill. This gets repetitive and the combat isn't as deep as it could be since combos are limited, and animations are repeated often. It does control well and feels smooth so I guess that's better than broken.
The most repetitive thing, and the game's biggest flaw, are the constantly repeated missions that repeat dozens and dozens of times. You can save citizens, do some time trial flag gathering missions, escort missions, assassination missions (probably the most fun), interrogation, eavesdropping, pickpocketing, and climbing tall buildings to find view points to put more missions on your map in that area. Sure they are fun at first, but after you have saved the 30th citizen, or climbed the 50th building it gets old and you just want it to end. Some more mission diversity would have been nice.
While its cool to be an assassin, sneaking up behind a guard and shoving a punch dagger in his gut, and then running away while he falls to the ground without anyone suspecting otherwise is satisfying you must look good doing it too. Assassin's Creed looks amazing, even today, and the PC version sports DirectX 10 graphics with some slightly higher resolution textures. The game looks a lot better than console versions and is well worth another play through just for that alone. While the graphics are amazing technically, artistically the game feels very Middle Eastern with a great soundtrack to support that, voice acting, and the whole game feels true to its time. The architecture is great, the clothing, lifestyles, and jobs people do in the game, but it all does kind of look the same with a lot of greys, browns, and whites.
Overall Assassin's Creed is an amazing experience with a story you will talk about long after you finish the game, great crowd simulation, and the true feeling of being an assassin. If there was some more mission diversity, visual diversity, and smoother controls the game would be perfect. This is a game you can not miss and every gaming fan should play this.
~Score: 8.5/10

Even though it really is in its early stages and has a somehow fancy comix-style grafic it is already fun. Your character (seedling) is until now genderless and ageing is not jet implemented,which makes him/her look as a child.But you will spend most of your time in ego-perspective anyway,since most actions require that.
You will be assisted in your early steps by a very good wiki,showing you all the tools and weapons and stuff you can craft and listing everything you need to do so.Should there arise questions the wiki can not jet answer, you will find an exceptionally friendly community which ,no doubt, will help you out.
Survival is not really hard: wherever you start your game you will find a large rock or even a boulder nearby with a hammerstone close to it,which you can pick up and use on the rock or boulder to get the stone parts of your first stone-age tools and weapons.Everything you need to make them will be close by.As soon as you have your stone sword you can face any aggressive animal which may cross you and get its hide and flesh if it has any and if you have at least a stone knive in your hand after the kill.
At that point I like to go exploring to harvest the different kinds of fruits (apples,cherries,melons,gourds,oranges,bananas and at least one pumpkin) .There are lots of them around ,so you are in no danger to starve: you eat them and get their seeds in your inventory ,which you later on may use to plant them close to your base (see the wiki for farming).Then I find a bit of sand (which later on I will use for crafting) and  since I like to make my first base in a cave,which will also be my mine and have a nice little garden with fruit-trees,gourds,melons and a pumpkin in it ,I look for a suitable place for it.
The place I look for allows me to mine horizontally into a rocky mountainface,while having enough space in front to work with my hoe to create my garden and sporting some tall trees nearby for the wood I will need.If I also can spot some goats to hunt nearby then I have found my place.
Since the game is in a very early stage,what you can do then is more or less set up your base with your crude bed and some workingplaces,mine for ore,hunt,cook,craft bronze tools and weapons and maybe build this and that minecraft-style.
For me so far it was fun and the money for the early access was well spent,and I see a lot of potential.

I haven't beaten the game yet, but from what I can tell so far, this game is not worth the cost of $35. I got it while it was on sale for $10 after having my eye on it since release, and I can't believe how many bugs and performance issues still persist in the game.
Pros
-The gameplay, when it works, can be really fun.
-The graphics are pretty good.
-Soundtrack is enjoyable to listen to.
Cons
-Aside from Shelly, the voice acting can range from bad to completely unbearable. Most of the random soldiers you encounter in the game have zero emotion and feel like they are bored while reading their lines. There's no sense of panic or urgency in their voices, which you would imagine they would feel when the earth has just been attacked by aliens.
-Some buggy animations, most notably with executions or enemy movement.
-The story, up to the point I'm at, is as bland and generic as it gets.
-The UI is absolutely horrible. While looking at your map, there appears to be no way to smoothly and easily look at the places you've been. You have to click and drag, and if you let go the map abruptly centers back on where your character is. The PIPboy-esque menu system is completely atrocious with no "back to previous menu" button which would make upgrading weapons much easier. Upgrading weapons feels laggy with the game responding 1-2 seconds after you click. It's also hard to tell which weaposn you can upgrade without spam clicking through them all to see what levels are required for the next upgrade.
-The balance feels awful. The Railgun upgrade you can get for your starting weapon (a weapon that auto regenerates ammo, by the way) very early into the game can one shot just about every non boss enemy. I've tried to use other weapons, or the "Bowling Bomb" grenades, but they just feel weak compared to the Railgun. It took about 12 Railgun shots to kill what I think was the first boss of the game, the "Abomination" and every other enemy has taken no more than 1.
-Powers feel mostly useless, aside from being used as a means to get around the map faster. Due to the aforementioned Railgun, there is no reason to use your powers to attempt to deal damage.
-Dying and choosing to respawn at the nearest checkpoint has a very high chance to wipe all of your explored map progress.
-Enemy AI is incredily buggy. Sometimes they will just stand there and do absolutely nothing, other times they will spam their jetpack / jump ability and get themselves stuck out of bounds. There is one enemy in particular that appears to be missing an animation. This enemy will stand completely still, and if you shoot at him, it reflects damage. You have no way to know that it's going to reflect damage until you've already shot at him and, if you're using the Railgun, either killed yourself or nearly killed yourself.
-Performance issues FPS drops down to 30 in some areas when there are a lot of enemys on screen. I've crashed at least 4 times in my 4 hours of playtime, which is annoying because sometimes I'll load int and all of my map exploration will have been reset. It also doesn't help that mid level checkpoints aren't very generous sometimes.
-Some upgrades (two of which I picked) are absolutely worthless, but you won't know they're absolutely worthless until you've already picked them. There is absolutely no way to reset weapon upgrades aside from starting an entire new game. Thankfully I chose the Railgun so I always have that to fall back on...
-Achievement progress is bugged. I've beaten episode 1 yet do not have the achievement for it. The achievements I have unlocked were spam unlocked upon returning to the main menu. The counters during gameplay are broken. Every time I die "This Isn't Dark Souls" pops up in the corner showing 1/50.
-Some weapons just don't do damage sometimes. Shelly's "Amiga" revolver decides half the time to just not do damage despite hitting the enemy. This is kind of funny considering based on screenshots the revolver seems to be one of her defining guns, yet it's utterly worthless in game.
All in all, after that huge list of cons with very minimal pros, I would never recommend this game for $35. Maybe if it goes back on sale for $10 it might be worth it, but not now.

[Rating: Four Dopefishes out of Five.] Despite its troubled release, Bombshell has been vigirously polished to become a damn fun game.
Some may frown at its hit-and-miss writing and voice work, as well as the occasional bug still lingering. Its side-quests and arena mini-game leave a little to be desired, too.
On the flip-side, it has some fantastic graphics and very well animated cut-scenes. Andrew Hulshult's music is a work of genius, with a movie-like soundtrack for cutscenes, creepy ambience for the calm before the storm, and some awesome action-packed tracks that deserve a place on your music player.
Its light-RPG mechanics are a nice touch, adding some more meat to the great combat. The shotgun, minigun, RPG and such are given some exotic names with oodles of great upgrades, from electrical blasts to stun enemies to multi-bombs for your homing Bowling Bombs (my favourite weapon). Combined with the special moves like the bubble shield and ground pound, it can make for some deadly combinations in battle.
The planets may seem a little stock at first, with a fire, ice and steel theme, but they make for some great exploration and look very well-designed. The ice planet has to be the best; you'll be having to dodge the icy pools, taking a merry boat ride, and plundering ancient ruins and icy plains for something to steal...or kill.
Interceptor really hit it out of the park with this one, especially thanks to the fixes and free content added alongside (Challenging "Shellshock" VR missions, a la Metal Gear Solid: Special Missions? Count me in!). Problems like unskippable executions and dialogue scenes no longer exist, either.
Snag it while you can, especially during a sale. It's great stuff.

Don't get me wrong, this game is gorgeous; the artwork is fantastic and there is some interesting gameplay. However, the majority of the game is filled with monotonous tasks, like climbing a wall, shimmying along a ledge, jumping to another ledge, shooting a switch to make a ladder fall so you can climb it. And when you're not climbing walls in a fashion that out dates the first 3d Prince of Persia game, you are fighting groups of enemies one after another with often no regard to the story.
The combat system is very simple and arcade like; you just chain together kick and punch moves, although you do gain some more abilities throughout the game like shooting enemies with some sort of digital hand thingy.
The best parts of the game where the scenery and the story, which unfortunately you are required to do a bunch of pointless boring tasks that just take up time and distract from the best parts of the game. At some points you can remix memories, which is actually really cool. You can rewind and fast forward through the memory and change subtle details that change the outcome.
All in all you are in a world that you will want to explore to no end, but you are stuck in the most linear gameplay that mostly has nothing interesting to offer. And although the mixing of memories thing is cool, I played the game for several hours and only got to do it once, and I got so frustrated and bored with the other elements of the game that I just uninstalled it.

I think the story of the game is unique but slow.  It's a shame to me how such a beautifully made world is limited to explore.   Our protagonist, Nilin, seems well rounded in character.  However, going back to being able to exploring the world, it seems odd how she can jump such great distances and parkour like a boss, yet she can't hurdle a 2ft wall.  The world is also not very interactive.  Only the items that will help you progress in the game's story (besides the boxes that boost your health and focus) can be interacted with.  I was expecting a reaction out of some of the robots when I punched or kicked them...nothing.  The same thing happens with the NPCs in Slum 404.  One thing that is a plus and minus is the camera angles.  When it comes to the parkour, some of the POVs are very helpful. Sometimes I couldn't see where I was supposed to jump to next because the computer took over my camera and I had no control of where I was looking (also happens when trying to get a glimpse at the surrounding city).  The architecture is amazing, and it's very hard to admire it because you see only what the designers want you to see.  If you want to play a CyberPunk game that is unique, play this one.  It is fun, but be warned that there is not a lot of freedom in where you go and what you can interact with.  It's good to play through once.  I don't see a point in playing through it again (unless you really want those pesky achievements).  Honestly, a bit of side questing, more interaction with the environment, and a bit more freedom would give this game a much higher replay value.  Just a thought if these developers ever read these things (highly doubt it).  Other than that it's a pretty good game...but for $30, wait until it's on sale.

Wow...This has to be the most visually stunning games I have ever played, but I won't lie and say the game play is flawless because it's not.  Combat is like an 'Arkham City wanna-be' but comes nowhere near the fluid motion of any of the Batman games.  But if you can get past the first few levels and upgrade your combos it's not so bad.  Actually once I quit trying to play it like Arkham and started playing it for what it was, I started to come around to the combat and enjoy a tad bit.  There are also plenty of platforming moments that are all pretty easy.  They mostly serve to break up the gameplay and show off a wider view of the levels, and let me tell you.....The world of Remember Me is the reason you want to play this game.  When you move from point A to B don't RUN...hold back on the thumbstick a bit and WALK and soak in every bit of the detail.  These guys have made one of the most beautiful games I have ever seen in my life.  The level to detail is staggering and is Remember Me's greatest asset.  That being said, I do wish they would have went the Splinter Cell route instead of the Arkham City route and had more focus on stealth.  This could have been the Starcraft Ghost that we never got.  Can you imagine?!?!?  Oh well, it's still a beautiful game and well worth a playthrough, especially if your a little burnt out on the same ol', same ol' Call of Duty or whatever mainstream game that usually takes up your time.  Do yourself a favor and give it a chance.  It doesn't cost much and worse case scenerio you just don't like it.  I think if you open your mind and look past the clunky combat, and look at the world instead you'll find it's actually damn good.

If you want a picture of the future, imagine a hand ripping out human memories - forever.
Remember Me envisions 2084 as a time when human memories can be manipulated like any physical item, and as such are bought, sold, traded, stolen, etc. much as physical items are. You control Nilin, a "memory hunter" - one with the power to manipulate human memories, up to and including large-scale rewrites. Recently wiped of most of her memories while in prison, she escapes and begins fulfilling tasks set to her by the Errorist known as Edge - a mysterious man who seeks the destruction of the privileged upper class the memory technology has created.
---
So, first off, the character design in this game is a bit lacking. Nilin isn't bad, but there's not a whole lot to really
about her, and no character, overall, is developed a whole lot - not helped by the fact that, due to the theme of memory manipulation, the whole concept of "character development" is harder to apply here.
The art style is well-done and the text design, in particular, is fantastic. Less can be said about the music, but at least it's not annoying. On a recommendation, I played with French voice acting, and I can pass on the recommendation - even if (like me) your knowledge of French is spotty at best, it helps with the recreation of the Neo-Paris atmosphere.
The gameplay...I mean, it's linear, and the combat system clearly has a lot of thought put into it, but gets rather repetitive regardless. Neither is inherently bad, but usually those are used in conjunction with a game focused on story, and that's where Remember Me falls a bit short.
The real killer is that the story premise is
quite interesting. Unfortunately, with the relatively short length and lack of character development, most of that potential doesn't go anywhere, and (very minor potential spoilers)
. Not at all what the asking price suggests about the game.
I still enjoyed my time with Remember Me, and if all of this has kept your interest so far, I'd advise you to give it a try (probably on sale, though). But if you're having your doubts? Nah.

作为免费的独立游戏完成度还可以，国产游戏更是要支持下，特别BGM还挺好，主要谈下我认为的问题
1.程序运行不流畅，经常卡顿，点个菜单、切换界面总要延时个半秒一秒的，很影响游戏心情。虽然我是办公电脑配置不高，A8 5600K+4G内存，64位win7，但这个画面怎么想应该只要是台能正常运行的电脑就应该能跑。而且不知道是个例还是普通的例子，我每运行半个到一个小时系统就要报次内存不足，甚至强迫我关掉浏览器，这就很奇怪了，平时哪怕我同时开几个word、excel、浏览器、QQ什么的把内存压榨完，也只是切换程序变慢，没出现过告警的，感觉这游戏的内存处理机制有问题。
2.UI问题很大。随便以给人物变更装备为例，先选中左侧“装备”标签，再单击确定-》右侧弹出人物选单，选中要更改装备的人物，单击确定-》选择“更换装备”-》选择要更换的类型，单击确定-》选中要变更的装备装上-》不要忘记鼠标右键退回你接下来要操作的那一级菜单，否则你做其它操作都是点不了的
繁琐吗？很繁琐，开始上手时总是奇怪为啥点这个没效，点那个没效，光就这一操作问题我就琢磨了一两分钟，搞懂以后，其实作为理科生我很欣赏这种严谨的条理逻辑，但作为游戏玩家，这种UI就相当的不友好不方便了。明明右侧就有人物头像，为啥我给法师换了法杖后不能直接点弓箭手头像切到妹子换弓箭？为啥我给一个人换好装备后不能直接点左侧标签看状态？如果是手柄操作还好点，但用鼠标操作不能所见所点所得就感觉相当憋屈。
另外战斗界面也有点繁琐，没有记住上一次的操作，没有撤退，没有直观的行动顺序，想全部平砍要么选攻击后还要用鼠标选攻击目标，要么还要腾出一只手拍键盘回车；敌人一多，要选中特定敌人有点困难，需要精细的操作。
3.既然是同一辆马车上的伙伴，又没有角色收集要素（玩到目前为止），战斗时只能出4个人没问题，但战斗经验能不能共享啊，结果就是没出场的两个人等级差越来越大，越没有出场机会，还不如一开始不要呢
4.大概是游戏性的问题，第一战还是第二战打小鹿老鹰什么的我就全体扑街了，啊？我日式RPG玩的少，这种史莱姆级别的不是送经验的吗？玩了两个小时后，大地图上的点都跑了一遍，还是在右边两个点练级刷小怪，怎么挖矿不知道，怎么挖蚯蚓钓鱼不知道，怎么推进剧情不知道……呃，我废都物语没玩过，是这个探索的味么？
5.一些小问题，大地图点左下马车图标，界面还没变过去呢，存档图标就变成床的图标了；买装备没有自动装备并卖掉原有装备选项；存档界面默认的焦点20号档位是自动存档吧？对于习惯从1号存档开始的人来说，因为显示的问题1234号存档还要往上滚下滚轮才操作得到
6.多加点妹子啊，一个六人队伍只有一个妹子说不过去啊（法师是男是女？），没妹子没动力，浪费美工啊

Wolfenstein: The New Order was a major surprise in 2014. I assumed it wouldn't be any good and was plesantly surprised by how great it was. The New Colosus had some big shoes to fill and I think it has done a spectacular job of living up to that legacy. Like the first game, the writing is top notch. The story and characters are as great as ever. Shooting is smooth and fun. Graphics are pretty great, though some character models look dated. Stealth is good in places but can often be obtuse and every segment relies too heavily on killing officers. Weapons are great if lacking in variety and the perk system from the first game is greatly improved to facility a play style that makes sense. Generally the New Colosus is a major improvement over the New Order and I highly recommend it. It's a solid 10 hour campaign with some fun bonus missions after the main story and DLC to come. If you're like me and enjoy a good single player shooter with a narrative focus you can't go wrong with Wolfenstein.

is a point & click adventure game. Although it usually isn't my preferred format for a review, in this case the text almost naturally grew into a 'pros and cons' list as I wrote it.
+ The voice acting is great. Really.
+ The backgrounds look nice. Not stunning but nice enough.
+ You play half of the game as Joe, a prisoner who wants to escape Alcatraz so he plans and prepares his escape from prison, and the other half of the game as Christine, Joe's girlfriend who's making the necessary 'outside' arrangements for the prison break from within the city of San Francisco. You can switch between the two characters at any time. This adds an interesting dynamic to the game and an extra dimension to the plot.
+ The actions you're required to perform in order to progress the story are very logical. Although, for some people this will mean the game is too easy.
+ You can press the space bar at any time to see the objects you can interact with in any scene. So if you're stuck, this can help. You don't have to use this feature and you can even switch it off entirely in the options menu.
+ Die-hard 1950s fans can choose to play the game in black & white by enabling '1954 mode' in the options menu.
- There's no real story branching until the very end where you make one of four choices that determine how the story ends right after that choice. Well, there are a few choices to be made earlier in the game but the only real difference this makes is whether or not you'll get the Steam Achievement
in the end.
- Character animation is ugly and clunky. When characters talk, their mouth just opens and closes rather fast as if they were a bunch of yapping muppets. And sometimes you can see a white void inside a character's head when (s)he's talking.
- There are no other animations besides character animation, so the world doesn't really feel 'alive'.
- Long loading times: every time you go from one scene to the next, the image either fades to black, which takes about 3 seconds, or freezes frame for about 4 seconds. After that, you see a black screen for about 3 seconds and then a black screen with a coffee cup to indicate the game is loading. So all in all, that's about 10 seconds each time, which is pretty long for a game like this.
- There are no puzzles at all in this game. I mean there is the standard point & click adventure gameplay (i.e. gathering items and using them on objects in the world or using them on other items in your inventory to combine them into a new item), of course, but there are no other/actual puzzles to be solved, unlike most other adventure games.
- I encountered a game-breaking bug near the end, which caused the game to tell me Christine's part was played and I couldn't switch to her anymore, whereas she still needed to do something that was absolutely required to advance Joe's side of the story. Luckily, I had a save from right before it happened or I would have been stuck before the game's final chapter could start.
- The game needs some tweaking to get the Steam Achievements working. I refer to the 'discussions' (forum) on Steam where you'll find the solution to this problem: disable Steam Overlay for the game and enable compatibility mode for the file 'Alcatraz.exe'. For me, running Windows 7 Home Premium 64 bit with Service Pack 1, I had to run the game in 'Windows 7' compatibility mode (so the non-SP mode).  The first achievement should trigger pretty much at the beginning of the game, after performing only a couple of actions and leaving your cell, so that's an easy way to check if achievements are working for you. If they're not, try a different compatibility setting and start a new game. Don't forget you won't see the achievements' pop-up like you may be used to (because you had to disable the overlay), so you need to alt-tab to Steam and check if the achievement triggered.

From the six hours I've played, I'd actually say I've enjoyed the story, gunplay, and presentation of The New Colossus. If you're a fan of The New Order and The Old Blood, then this won't disappoint on that front. However, I would strongly recommend that you don't pick this game up at present. The game has a variety of technical issues (I experienced some frustrating crashing myself that I fixed by trying a number of random fixes, installing new drivers, and rebooting a bunch) that make it somewhat difficult to recommend at present.
The biggest issue that I am aware of, and that effected me personally, is that patches will reset your progress in ongoing levels. I had put quite a bit of time into a level, downloaded the update, and then found out that I'd have to replay the whole thing. This is ludicrous and quite frustrating. No thanks. I'll probably change my review to a recommended after they stop updating the game and adding DLC, but for the time being, leave it alone.

I lost interest in The New Order and The Old Blood about halfway through each, but this one I played all the way through and I love it. The New Colossus has many flaws, but it's hard not to be charmed by its over-the-top weirdness. There's so many moments that I can honestly say I've never seen in a game before.
The combat is fast and brutal. You can find hidden weapon upgrades that slightly increase your power throughout the game, but for the most part it's a standard weapon set. You can also scavenge for big guns that use wall chargers. Stealth is very difficult, but it's satisfying just to take down a few guards before the alarms go off. The environments all look great, but I found myself getting lost fairly often and getting stuck on invisible walls.
The cast of characters have frustrating quirks, but these often play out to great affect when they clash or cooperate. Not all the jokes land, but there's some genuinely hilarious moments. The cut scene editing is excellent and keeps the story moving at a perfect pace. And then there's a moment in the middle that I won't spoil which is one of the single greatest twists I've ever seen in a game. My jaw dropped and it still makes me laugh when I think about it.
There's tones of secrets in the game: diaries, concept art, cards, etc. I didn't find any of this compelling because I mostly mashed the pick-up button while sprinting through environments. But they have a nice in-fiction system for returning to previous levels and collectors can significantly extend the game's lifetime.
The run and gun aspects are a little repetitive by the end, and the conclusion is very abrupt and unsatisfying, but I was toughly entertained despite its stumbles.

From a purely gameplay perspective, this game is dissappointing when compared to Wolfenstein: The New Order.  The gun play, character development, and overall story arc is just... meh.  The new dual wielding system is a welcome touch, as are the new hatchet takedowns.  Other than those two additions, the rest of the game is very lackluster compared to TNO.  BJ feels like an unstoppable UberMensch at the lower difficulties while feeling like a wet rag on higher difficulties where most enemies kill you in one second of stepping out of cover.  The AI is very good.  They work together well and challenge you tactically, which is what they should do.  However, once alerted, they are aware of your location 24/7 and you don't have any chance to flank around them as they will already be rushing to meet you at your new corner.  You could backtrack to the beginning of the level and take an alternate path, only to be met by all the enemies you thought you bamboozled.  To sum it up, the gunplay of TNC leaves a lot to be desired when compared to TNO.
The second problem with TNC, is the story.  It is flat.  There is no direction and it feels like a jumbled mess at times.  The characters are far more cliche now than they were in the first one.  There is a black revolutionary, a communist/marxist revolutionary, and... BJ.  BJ is now a texan who can really only make quick quips about how evil the Nazi's are, or about his family.  They took a character who had a decent amount of complexity from TNO and just made him a guy who shoots things.  There are a few character deaths in the story that should have made an impact, but really didn't.  The game climaxes at the end when you kill the BBEG, and that's it.  There isn't a great bossfight like in TNO.  There are a few bad guys between you and the final cutscene, which is just that, a cutscene.  It felt very rushed, and beating the game on 2nd hardest difficulty only took 8 hours (the hardest is locked), whereas in TNO it took close to 20, but TNO is a much better game than TNC.  If you liked TNO, you may be dissappointed with TNC.

I have put many hours into Skullgirls, not just on steam but also at other friends houses and on consoles. I have to say it is honestly my favorite fighting game and I absolutely love fighting games, so that's obviously pretty high praise coming from me.
Game Mechanics: Skullgirls has one of the most interesting fighting game systems i've ever seen. The 5 layered system of how combos are performed before a burst can be activated is insanely smart as it limits the potentional for cheap exploitable gimmicks like infinites. Trust me, I love a good infinite as much as the next guy but it can really slow down the pace of a game like Marvel 3 where damage scaling is a thing. Overall, the way teams are set up isn't that new of a concept if you've played games like Marvel VS Capcom or Capcom VS SNK but what is new that I haven't noticed in any other fighting game, is the ability to set your teams assist to anything. If you want your teammate to come out and taunt(because taunts aren't just for showboating in this game) you can totally do that. That alone can keep the game really fresh because you won't always see people rocking the same assist on a character that you see everywhere else. Overall mechanicaly, I think this game is absolutely stellar!
Sound: Skullgirls features a great voice cast with many unique lines and even alternate voice packs for certain characters, my favorite being Big Band's Sax-ploitation not only because of the lines but also the pun in the name. It also features one of my favorite soundtracks of a fighting game. Not all the tracks are amazing but it certainly has some standouts like "Unfinished Business" "NMO Arena" and the absolutely fantastic credits song "In Just a Moment's Time".
Art: Skullgirls has some of the best 2D character art i've seen in a long time. Of course it will never beat sprite art like SF3: 3rd Strike or FF6 but those are all-timers. It also has about 25 colors for every character, some that may even be a bit familiar depending on what games you've played in the past, however you have to buy the color pack to unlock most colors but I personally think it's worth it. The games menus are all presented in an old school, film-fed projector style giving it the feeling of a movie. Main menus: film reel. Character select: film reel. Match start: film reel. Everytime a super is used: film reel. This attention to detail and consistency really shows how much love was put into the presentation of this game. Not to mention the full fledged art gallery of concept art and professional art by comissioned artists for each character and stage that continues to unlock as you play the game.
Overall: I think if you are any kind of fighting game fan at all you should definitely pick this, even if you're not I think it's worth a go! If you're stingy you can get this game for a little under $4(with all DLC it's about $8) on a pretty regular basis. However if you really feel like supporting the developers you can get it for $15 plus if you wanna buy the DLC. I've bought 3 copies of this game including a physical copy shipping to me in January, because I love it so much and if you end up buying it I hope you love it too!

Firstly, I would like to applaud the developers at Nerd Kingdom on a great job in developing a terrific game so far.  It must be, I’ve logged over 900 hours since purchasing the game in September 2014. Apparently, I don’t have a life.  To put this into perspective, that’s about 6 hours of game playing per day over the past five months.
Like most people, I enjoy playing open world sandbox survival games, exploring, crafting, mining, but mostly building things.  TUG offers all of these things, but with a very rich non-blocky interactive environment where you become immersed into your surroundings. The world ambient sounds seem to add to this immersion, leading you to start foraging for supplies right away to survive at least the first night.  The environment sounds have you looking over your shoulder for critters that might be sneaking up on you or a sound that stops you in your tracks wondering what is that?, is it going to eat me?, do I run away?
Once you start the game, you immediately find yourself exploring or running away from a critter because you haven’t crafted a weapon yet and thinking that the rock in your hand doesn’t seem adequate enough to defend yourself, or just wanting to see what is over the next hill or to watch a spectacular sunrise or sunset.  Once you feel safe you notice that you are now hungry so you begin foraging for food to eat.  My mom always wanted me to be a vegetarian.  You now notice that your backpack of many things is full containing mostly different types of rocks, a few sticks and some vines. You begin throwing these items onto the ground to see what can be crafted. Now that you are armed to the teeth with stone tools and weapons; including a hoe and shovel, you are more likely to begin building something such as a hole in the ground to hide in or experimenting with the various available building materials (limited at the moment) to construct your dream home-base to venture forth from into the world of TUG.

One thing I like about TUG so far is that there are no zombies, yet.  I don’t like zombies as they sneak-up on you while you are busy doing something and scare the ___ out of you, much like the forest children do in this game, the kinokojin.

Although I have experienced many game crashes mostly with the indev version, lost files, and other game bugs, TUG is still a great game so far and knowing it will get even better with future updates.

Putting all that aside, the following are some suggestions that would be nice to see implemented into the game; however, some of these suggestions may not be possible:
1.	Crafting a compass. This is not really necessary, but crafting a compass would be a cool way to explore the world of TUG for those who need one.  Based on your compass marches or hikes, you could craft area maps.  I found that knowing where the sun rises and sets in the game (east and west) and using landmarks, whether made or natural, you can navigate throughout the world quite reasonably.

2.	Crafting a bow and arrows.
3.	The gathering and or crafting of new building materials.
4.	Doors, windows and furniture.
5.	Adding a smaller block size in addition to the two we already have for adding building trim details.
6.	Once water is introduced into the game, will seedlings be able to swim?
7.	Crafting a boat to float down that lazy river or to see if you can survive boating over a waterfall or white water rafting.
8.	Crafting a fishing rod to go fishing on that hot sunny afternoon.  Crafting different types of lures or using different types of bait to attract different types of fish would be cool.  Fishing could also be dependent on the time of day and the weather.
9.	Climbing trees to get away from predators when all you have is a rock in your hand to defend yourself.  The only problem with this type of defence is that the predator will not go away and you will eventually starve to death sitting in the tree, unless you can eat the tree leaves. Picture the scene from the Movie ‘Quest for Fire’.
10.	Throw rocks, especially at tigers and the forest children.
11.	Pets, a dog like creature, horse or riding type creature.
12.	Other wildlife critters to hunt or to just watch, such as ungulates, birds and predator type creatures.
13.	Different mystical biome creatures, one for each type of biome.
14.	More world ambient sounds, such as a hooting owl in the haunted forest biome, howling critters when the moon rises, etc.
15.	Weather systems such as rain, snow, thunder storms, tornados, etc.
16.	More uses for critter hides other than leather strips.
17.	Crafting implements of destruction such as a trebuchet or canon to silent that noisy forest child, just kidding.
In closing, all I can say about TUG is that it is an awesome game so far and has the potential of being one of the best open world sandbox survival games presently being developed.
All the best to the developers at Nerd Kingdom and keep up the great work.

Although this game is literally a clone of Diablo 3 (and when I say literally, I mean even the ranking of the enemies, their health colour bars and their pack numbers are the same as Diablo 3), I would still go as far as saying that this is one of the best Diablo clones out there.
The Good:
1. The game plays like Diablo 3, but the look and feel of the game is more like Diablo 2. So, all Diablo fans who hated D3 for looking too colourful like Warcraft, play this instead.
2. Enemies once wiped out don't respawn. I mean, yes, we enjoyed that in Diablo, D2 and even in D3, and a lot of people would say its not a good thing, but I have no interest in exploring the game's mechanics (having played all Diablo games several times). I'd rather just follow the story mission by mission, than having to clear the same areas repeatedly, and get frustrated.
3. Each mission area / level is lot smaller than it is in and of the Diablo games. Most people won't find it great when it comes to the main quest, but it REALLY helps with the side quests. Exploring a random cave in Diablo 1, 2 or 3 was sooooooooo boring! You'd go through all of those tunnels, just for the loot. Not even a quest. At least in Diablo 3, Blizzard introduced Events, which quests activated inside the tunnels.
The Bad:
- Van Helsing is a medieval monster slayer. The hero of Bram Stoker's Dracula. A goddamn legend, up until Hollywood detroyed that legend and the the Twilight series even destroyed vampires and werewolves. Medeival lore is full of content which could have been used to create missions, dialog and fresh pop cultural refrences. Instead, the game uses stale, existing pop culture to bond with the player, like an NPC saying,
"I used to be a monster slayer like you, then I took... ummm... nothing."
Stale and lame.
All in all, Van Helsing is a good game, but it could have been a great game, if the devs had worked upon the content. If you're wanting to buy it, I should tell you that I bought the pack of all three games + DLC for less than $3 on the summer sale.

Having finished Bombshell, I can readily understand why it has mixed reviews. It's a well-presented top-down, mouse-aim shooter with a a diverse range of weapons and abilities, classic action shooter sensibility and a smattering of elements from FPSs, RPGs and platformers that more or less work well together, but it's also a rather messily executed pile of bugs, occassionally of the game-breaking variety. It reminds me of nothing if not EYE: Divine Cybermancy in this regard. Enemies disappearing, Shelly getting stuck in places, weird jump physics, mission critical items not being able to be picked up, preventing progress... most egregiously, completing the quest to get the final weapon in the game bugged, and I had no weapon to show for it. I have played a dozen games like Bombshell that weren't half as broken.
It also drags a bit, padding out it's approximately nine hours of campaign play with oddly spaced checkpoints and forced backtracking to complete sidequests. The combat balance is also odd, with Shelly's power sword ability outperforming most of her firearms. It has an interesting "splitting" mechanic with Shelly's AI-controlled arm, Amiga, being able to detach itself and move independantly of her, but this mechanic is only occasionally used for puzzle solving, and this game has the barest minimum of puzzle difficulty akin to the Duke Nukem games, barring one painful riddle for which the solution can be found here on Steam in the game's only current guide.
That being said, it has lovely visuals and it is obvious that this game had a lot of heart put into it, and it has been patched since launch- which makes me wonder how badly it ran when it first released. One would hope the forthcoming 1.3 patch will address more of these issues. I got it on sale for about $12, which is a reasonble price. As it is, the base price of thirty is far too steep for what you get.
It's quite obvious that it was meant to be a Duke Nukem game, but it's honestly better as is. Shelly Harrison is a more interesting character with actual development and internal conflict, rather just Duke with breasts, as her canceled appearance in Duke Nukem Forever might have portrayed her. The music is excellent, and while the NPC voice actors were really phoning it in, Shelly's own VA is pretty good.
I'm honestly on the fence about Bombshell. If you love top-down shooters as much as I do you will probably find something to like in this game, but if you're a stickler for bug-free gaming you'll want to look elsewhere.

+ It's got a nice riffing soundtrack
- Feels a little low-budget, like it needed more polish

Wolfenstein: The New Order was a major surprise in 2014. I assumed it wouldn't be any good and was plesantly surprised by how great it was. The New Colosus had some big shoes to fill and I think it has done a spectacular job of living up to that legacy. Like the first game, the writing is top notch. The story and characters are as great as ever. Shooting is smooth and fun. Graphics are pretty great, though some character models look dated. Stealth is good in places but can often be obtuse and every segment relies too heavily on killing officers. Weapons are great if lacking in variety and the perk system from the first game is greatly improved to facility a play style that makes sense. Generally the New Colosus is a major improvement over the New Order and I highly recommend it. It's a solid 10 hour campaign with some fun bonus missions after the main story and DLC to come. If you're like me and enjoy a good single player shooter with a narrative focus you can't go wrong with Wolfenstein.

From the six hours I've played, I'd actually say I've enjoyed the story, gunplay, and presentation of The New Colossus. If you're a fan of The New Order and The Old Blood, then this won't disappoint on that front. However, I would strongly recommend that you don't pick this game up at present. The game has a variety of technical issues (I experienced some frustrating crashing myself that I fixed by trying a number of random fixes, installing new drivers, and rebooting a bunch) that make it somewhat difficult to recommend at present.
The biggest issue that I am aware of, and that effected me personally, is that patches will reset your progress in ongoing levels. I had put quite a bit of time into a level, downloaded the update, and then found out that I'd have to replay the whole thing. This is ludicrous and quite frustrating. No thanks. I'll probably change my review to a recommended after they stop updating the game and adding DLC, but for the time being, leave it alone.

I lost interest in The New Order and The Old Blood about halfway through each, but this one I played all the way through and I love it. The New Colossus has many flaws, but it's hard not to be charmed by its over-the-top weirdness. There's so many moments that I can honestly say I've never seen in a game before.
The combat is fast and brutal. You can find hidden weapon upgrades that slightly increase your power throughout the game, but for the most part it's a standard weapon set. You can also scavenge for big guns that use wall chargers. Stealth is very difficult, but it's satisfying just to take down a few guards before the alarms go off. The environments all look great, but I found myself getting lost fairly often and getting stuck on invisible walls.
The cast of characters have frustrating quirks, but these often play out to great affect when they clash or cooperate. Not all the jokes land, but there's some genuinely hilarious moments. The cut scene editing is excellent and keeps the story moving at a perfect pace. And then there's a moment in the middle that I won't spoil which is one of the single greatest twists I've ever seen in a game. My jaw dropped and it still makes me laugh when I think about it.
There's tones of secrets in the game: diaries, concept art, cards, etc. I didn't find any of this compelling because I mostly mashed the pick-up button while sprinting through environments. But they have a nice in-fiction system for returning to previous levels and collectors can significantly extend the game's lifetime.
The run and gun aspects are a little repetitive by the end, and the conclusion is very abrupt and unsatisfying, but I was toughly entertained despite its stumbles.

From a purely gameplay perspective, this game is dissappointing when compared to Wolfenstein: The New Order.  The gun play, character development, and overall story arc is just... meh.  The new dual wielding system is a welcome touch, as are the new hatchet takedowns.  Other than those two additions, the rest of the game is very lackluster compared to TNO.  BJ feels like an unstoppable UberMensch at the lower difficulties while feeling like a wet rag on higher difficulties where most enemies kill you in one second of stepping out of cover.  The AI is very good.  They work together well and challenge you tactically, which is what they should do.  However, once alerted, they are aware of your location 24/7 and you don't have any chance to flank around them as they will already be rushing to meet you at your new corner.  You could backtrack to the beginning of the level and take an alternate path, only to be met by all the enemies you thought you bamboozled.  To sum it up, the gunplay of TNC leaves a lot to be desired when compared to TNO.
The second problem with TNC, is the story.  It is flat.  There is no direction and it feels like a jumbled mess at times.  The characters are far more cliche now than they were in the first one.  There is a black revolutionary, a communist/marxist revolutionary, and... BJ.  BJ is now a texan who can really only make quick quips about how evil the Nazi's are, or about his family.  They took a character who had a decent amount of complexity from TNO and just made him a guy who shoots things.  There are a few character deaths in the story that should have made an impact, but really didn't.  The game climaxes at the end when you kill the BBEG, and that's it.  There isn't a great bossfight like in TNO.  There are a few bad guys between you and the final cutscene, which is just that, a cutscene.  It felt very rushed, and beating the game on 2nd hardest difficulty only took 8 hours (the hardest is locked), whereas in TNO it took close to 20, but TNO is a much better game than TNC.  If you liked TNO, you may be dissappointed with TNC.

Really enjoyed this one. It's another point and click adventure, but this one's put out by Daedalic, who made a name for themselves with the terminally on sale Deponia series. This game has a fine level of polish and some legitimate character to it. Everyone is voice acted, the setting is relatively unique, and it just feels considerably more alive than a lot of other adventure games that I could think of.
On top of that, the story is actually pretty intriguing, which is fairly high praise. I don't anticipate it blowing my mind or anything, but it's honestly not all that often that you run across a game that focuses on breaking a person out of prison (let alone alcatraz) from both inside and outside of the facility. There's even a sense that I could influence certain outcomes in the earliest parts of the game depending on dialogue choices, suggesting that this would be good for some replay material. I probably won't, but the thought is nice.
I think the thing I like most about this game is that even though the environments are cluttered as hell, they allow you to press spacebar to see all the items you may interact with. That's design that has learned from the nightmares of the Sierra era in adventure/p&c games. Don't get me wrong, I still fondly remember those games (and will have to play them again eventually in this project) but the idea of actually playing them again is not one of my favorites.
The puzzles also seem pretty logical. I'm not super deep into the game yet, but this seems more along the lines of a modern telltale style adventure game rather than anything from the genre's spotty past. It's a pretty quality product and I'm actually pretty glad I'm finally giving it a shot.

I haven't had this much fun causing mischief since Thief 2.
Assassin's Creed is, at its heart, a series of minigames. 1) Scale towers to get a look around; 2) eavesdrop; 3) fight city guards who are harrassing citizens; 4) interrogate know-it-alls; 5) pick pockets; and above all, 6) run like heck from city guards until you can ditch them in a cart full of hay, a rooftop gazebo, or blend in on a bench. But there is variety in these challenges, and all of this is stitched together with the most beautiful sandbox cities since GTA IV. You set your own pace in this gorgeous game.
My complaints are few: no indoor environments in cities, too much late-game swordplay, and dreadfully long mandatory cutscenes.
Lastly, AC offers fluid swordplay, and a parkour-like experience scrambling over rooftops. It's just fun to play, and the right length.  Thumbs up.

Very nice game. I didn't play this when it came out but I picked it up while on sale and it would have well been worth full price. This game reminds me of a mashup of Prince of Persia + Assasin's Creed.
A really really really cool idea in this game is the "memory remix" puzzles, where you basically rewind time and mess with different objects and then press play and watch what happens. Moving different items at different times produces different results and you have to get the right order to cause the memory to continue with the desired outcome. I hate that there are so few of these because it is the standout feature of this game and I would jump to play a full game full of these types of missions.
Fighting is not the main objective but basically a means of showing progression through the very interesting story.
It has a unique although hard to get used to combat system, similar to the Assasin's Creed games although not so timed and it is harder to dodge. It has all the fun parkour of Assasin's creed with fun Prince of Persia style jumping puzzles.
A great game I would definitely recommend. Perhaps it will encourage them to create a new game or reuse some of the aspects of this game in a future title.

I understand the negative reviews pertaining to the performance and agree that MachineGames could have polished things a little better. I had the crash dump error when the game released, but after adding a firewall rule for the Wolf2 .exe I haven't experienced crashing or any other issues.
I do not agree with the negative reviews pertaining to the game's supposed political stance. First, development has likely been going on for several years, so the story is not meant to represent or relate to current events. Second, the story is an alternate history in which the Nazis won WWII. It is likely to broach some sensitive subjects, and I think some are feeling a little bit too entitled in regards to telling MachineGames what they can and cannot put into their own game to tell this story. Third, I believe the game should be distinct from the marketing stance Bethesda took prior to launch.
Ultimately, I can recommend this game as a great story with good combat.
