Despite teasing you with interesting environments like 60s Nazi controlled Roswell during a parade, they drop you into generic Nazi base #287 instead. This is the case throughout the entire campaign.
The game is riddled with bugs. It runs well over 60fps for me, with very rare dips, but there are occasional graphical glitches. Like the New York skyline not loading, leaving just a black box in the sky. The game freezes during loading far too often.
And to top it all off, they release the first update and it's somehow not compatible with your save data, you have to start over from the beginning of whatever chapter you were on. Which could be an hour+ of time wasted.

Honestly, I really don't want to do this, but at it's current state for Nvidia GeForce GTX 980 Ti, with the updated drivers, it's pretty much crash city.
So far, I was in love with this game, it looks fantastic, the controls are fairly simple, the story is excellent if you're following up from TNO, voice acting's brilliant, and the atmosphere in the game is second to none.
But, it has it's flaws, just like every other game.
As said before, the game crashes.  When does it?  Well, there's a chance to crash between loading screens.  Especially as you've gotten... what, halfway? (tiny spoiler)  When you're given a new body, and the Eva's Hammer's Map.  As soon as you try to choose an Ubercommander's location and hit accept, the screen goes black, and it locks up the pc, bar Ctrl Alt Del. Which I have done the past 4 or 5 times.
The weapons are sub par too.  Once again, don't get me wrong, the design of them are fantastic, but there's so little in the way of weaponry that it feels awkward, so to speak.  Most of the time, I find myself using the shotgun or the rifle, when I initially use the silenced pistol.  There's the lack of a proper sniper rifle/marksman rifle, which could've gotten carried over from TNO.  And you have to find weapon upgrade kits to upgrade each weapon, including the heavy weapons, three times.  Sure, it unlocks good potential, but I found myself using them on the shotty or the assault rifle, which I really didn't want to, but they were the only decent upgrades at the time.  THAT BEING SAID, the weapons all control well, and getting a long range hatchet kill is always satisfying.
So, all I can really say is that until they fix the black screen of zombification in the loading screens, it's playable up to a point, then you can't play no more.  Until they fix it, I'd say play through The Old Blood and The New Order again.
TL;DR version: Please fix the BSOZ, and when you do, I can put out a proper review.  But for now, Avoid.
UPDATED REVIEW:
So, after looking up a way to try and fix the game, it turned out that apparently, I didn't have all the files.  This only occured when someone said to "Click on "Verify the Integrity of the files" in the options page."  Which is what I did, and with that, it has allowed me to go further than before when it was BSOZ'ing on me.  So far, I can safely say that the game is now in working order, and the only problem I've had with it running was being blasted out of the game by one of the Ubercommanders.  I'm not sure if this was supposed to happen, but I found it hilarious none the less.
Weapons opinion is still the same, but the contraptions you get are entertaining, and they all have an upside, and a very simple thing to do to get their small upgrades, so I guess I can put those under the plus side.
Other than that, the review is relatively the same, but I can safely say that if you're looking for a good time waster, with a lot of character, a lot of backstory, and one hell of an atmospheric trip, then go right ahead and buy it, or wait for a sale for it if the price is too steep for you.  If it is, once again, get the two previous games and have a blast on those, then when you can, give this a shot.
TL;DR 2: Just make sure that all files are where they should be, run "View Integrity of Files" or w/e it's called, let it do it's thing, then play.  Then you'll be good to go around and slaughter several nazis.
Final Verdict: BUY (or BUY IF ON SALE, DEPENDING ON HOW STRAPPED FOR CASH YOU ARE).

Painter's Guild is a little management, simulation, time management game. If you can get it at a lowered price it's worth it, given that you like games in that spectrum at all of course.
For such a small game in retro pixel graphic style it's rather complex. You can change the look of your painters to your liking with a dresser, you can decorate & furnish the rooms which increases the comfort for the painters, improves their skilling options & elevates the prestige of the guild, which then attracts richer clients. The painters you hire have a quite complex personality as well, there are two traits, both painting related which make the painter either faster painting, quicker skilling, healthier, easier to get into trouble & prison, painting more beautifully or changing quicker the initial painting style ... Besides of painting at the easels painters can also work outside the guild on murals, which pays better but is strenous enough to even kill your painters. There are three options to hire new painters, from cheapest & immediately arriving to most expensive & requiring some time for the painter to arrive & you're also able to hire some of the greatest painters of that time like Leonardo daVinci & Michelangelo Buonarotti. You hire the painters at a very young age, often as teenagers, after having some training at the guild they go on a journey, come back & skill further, can become a master painter, become even more skilled, age, get gray hair, become ill & die. In that respect it is quite a depressing game, the time is flowing, the masters which you trained & nurtured over the in game years are just gone one day & your guild is left without them & may not be able to provide paintings anymore of similiar quality, unpaid apprentices may even leave the guild & you will be left with the remaining handful of journeymen.
I noticed only one bug so far. Sometimes the easel with the painting gets stuck somewhere, making all clicks irresponsive. Though i was able to come out of that bug without loosing the progress, it's still unnerving.
Overall highly recommended.

Painters Guild is a litle flash(? not sure but looks like one) game that can easily cost you a few hours to play. Yet I cant recommend it.
The game itself is pretty shallow, grindy and the end absolutle unsatisfying. You just play until you reach 1620 and then ... "here is your highscore you can stop playing now... or go on ... we dont care".
The game itself is pretty shallow as well. You just organize your painters meaning 99% of the time you will simply be rotating them from the sofa/bed to the paintings or to the current training items. The idea of training your painters in different styles and "go with fashion" is interesting enough, only that this mechanic does not work. It takes a painter way to long to change his style and it does not give you that much of a benefit (20% more gold). In the time it takes to change the painting style he could have finished 2-3 paintings and thus earning way more gold than the current style bonus... especially as this changes often faster than the painter can learn new styles.
Other than that there is next to no decision makeing on your part. Furniture? Buy the best your money allows. Painters? Train to 100 skill and swap them between paintings and sofas. Great works (like painting a cathedral) are a nice idea but the mechanic is utterly broken as well. Why? Those works have a top payout of 250 gold and can take 3-6 of your painters away for up to 1 in game year. As a comparison. A single painting worked on for 3 months with 2 painters will net you the nearly same ammount of gold. And the reputation hits you take for turning away customers while doing a great work is not even nearly compensated by the reputation gained from doing the great work.
So in the end the game has some interesting concepts but they all suffer from unbalanced (not broken) mechanics that simply makes those concepts unfun to engage with because they actively punish the player for engaging.
The most effective way of playing is to only spend time and effort on finishing paintings and training painters.
I spend 8 hours with the game and that will probably all the time of my life I spend playing it.
Is that worth the 9,99€ asked price? Hell no. I couldnt even recommend getting this at a 50% sale. There is just to litle fun to be had here. There is no strategy no clever thinking required, all there is to do is grind grind grind until you reach a boring highscore message.

, another gem designed by Hidden Object Games (HOG) masters, Artifex Mundi, offers a lot of story at a reasonable enough pace. The game can be completed in under 5 hours, on expert mode, so it's not too demanding where you can't still play it casually. Does that even make sense...?
The story begins in a small town known as Hochwald - presumably somewhere in Germany. While a once peaceful town, you will quickly find that that is the case no more. Agent Evangelie Glass is summoned by her friend and mentor, Dr. Ink, who is on a mission to uncover the mysterious secrets of the Barber family. Hochwald has, ultimately, been plagued by increasingly powerful tremors, and Dr. Ink has landed himself in trouble by attempting to sabotage "master inventor Barber", the latter of whom does not have the town in his best interest. With the help of a little mechanical bird, named Matthew, do you have what it takes to thwart Barber's evil plans?
+  If you're into them, achievements are very easy to obtain
+  The graphics are easily some of the best that I have seen for a HOG
+  The way the story is laid out is good. It is paced evenly and nothing was rushed
+  Voice acting was done extremely well - one of them did make me go, "really?", however
+  Hopefully you don't find the puzzles too difficult. On average, they probably took me about 3 minutes to do. However... (continued in neutral)
+  Play with the music and sound on - do as they recommend; it is amazing and you can tell that they really put in a lot of effort to create a good audio experience for the player
±  ... one of the puzzles was giving me trouble and I couldn't get past it for a good 20 minutes. Lack of instructions wasn't too helpful (no kidding), but I eventually got through it
-  The game is extremely short. Even after playing the 2nd half of the game -
- I still ended up with a completion time of under 4 hours. So I would recommend only getting this game once it's bundled or under $2.00
-  I know this is steampunk, but some of the items felt really out of place, especially for the time period. It's like they attempted to fit the 1600s in with some 2010 elements. I can't remember what item I saw (it was during a hidden object scene), but it made me question the time frame; there were actually a few items
While on your mission to save Dr. Ink and the whole town from thheir demise, you will uncover a beautifully told story, wonderful adventures,  and stunning graphics. Give it a good go, and
will most definitely not disappoint.
Overall:

8.5/10 Very casual game, but a lot of fun all the same. I really enjoyed the steampunk style and the voice acting was surprisingly good. The amount of gameplay you get is not very long unless you try to get all of the achievements (which I did). I also did some of this while eating lunch or dinner, so I was able to eke out a little more time. It's definitely worth the money, because you also get an extra hour of gameplay playing an additional story that prequels the original once you're finished with the first game. For those who are wondering this is the Collector's Edition which is normally sold for twice the price at other download sites.

- Great art, especially the backgrounds and that clockwork bird.

- If you like hidden object games, you might be a little disappointed since the game is mostly puzzles.
Definitely recommend, and I look forward to seeing more in this series.

The graphics are amazing, the trailers entice you with a warm inviting embrace and it looks fun enough to play, although it's a trap. A massive, trap for me in the very least.
The game starts out innocent enough as you're learning the ropes but as you progress you have 4 modes of play that are horrendously repetitive.
1. Combat, wholly dependent on combos, bland and obvious. Use X skill to disarm Y enemies shield, use Z combo to cooldown skills and repeat. Dodging is easy enough, but clunky and basically... just going through motions.
2. Assassin's creed style springboard jumping through the city ala la spiderman in a tutu minus the webs and emphasis on parkour. 90% of it is linear, it's usually obvious where to go. Mild old school platiformer patience of wait 3 seconds, memorize pattern, then proceed to dodge but there's so few of these areas. Some areas are insta-gib and unforgiving.
3. Puzzles of manipulating memories and very weak riddles of pure trial and error with no semblance of what's going on. Basically poke a dead donkey and see what happens, poke it somewhere else and repeat until desired results occur.
4. Stealth element is luke-warm MetalGear-esque. It isn't fun, nor is it a challenge. There's pretty much only one way through most of them.
So, in the end what's this game have going for it? Concept and storyline. Props for being ballsy to try something new in a stagnant market of meme-sheepage zombie/warcraft etc games. It tried to be like Deus Ex, but has nothing that made the game fun. It COULD have been amazing if it wasn't some clunky mix-mash. Get it cheap, get it for the storyline, the philosophy, the perceptive of life and politics but if you want a game that can really draw you in and have replay value, steer clear.

It's rare to find a game with such an enthralling story that doesn't sacrifice gameplay for a "movie-experience," and yet this game had me playing almost non-stop throughout precisely because every moment left me wanting more. The combat provided smooth intermissions that were engaging and satisfying for a video-game experience, and the characters and story drove me to continue traversing the ambient environment for further understanding. "Remember Me" is a great game and definitely a worthwhile buy if you are at all considering it.

Remember Me has a story quite rich and interesting about personal memory controlling within a world very immersive and well portrayed in a beautifully crafted cyberpunk Neo-Paris artwork. It's a third person beat'em up that is sure action packed with stunning visuals and a memorable storyline (no pun intended). One of my most favorite underrated games ever.

One of, if not the most, disappointing games of 2017.
The New Colossus starts out incredibly strong, with a killer opening level where you're rolling around on a wheelchair, shooting Nazis down staircases and up conveyor belts. It feels just like a continuation of The New Order, and that's a great thing. There's a stronger emphasis on cutscenes and storytelling, but this first level handles it extremely well, and I was absolutely gripped.
Then, the rest of the game happens.
There's a level where you're on the prowl in a radioactive wasteland, somewhat similar to Fallout 3, and your health's constantly decreasing; you jump from Nazi to Nazi to survive, scavenging armor and health packs on the way, and witnessing bodies of hundreds of irradiated civilians is an extremely somber experience. It motivates you to fight, to rebel, which is the overarching them of the game. Then you meet a sassy black lady who outmanuevers you, comments on how "only the Blacks have been fighting the Nazis," whips out her baby and starts breastfeeding it while giving a debriefing, mocks you and all your crew, and takes up a cabin of one of your dead allies, all within *five minutes* of her introduction.
It's a bit of a tonal shift.
The rest of the game suffers from this issue. It feels like the script was written by three different people: one who really wanted to push the envelope as far as story in a FPS is handled, who understood the characters of The New Order and wanted to explore *why* they fight and *what* they're fighting for, one who's there to make sure the story appeals to people who feel bitter about Trump, who does their damndest to make sure that for every sincerely touching moment, Sassy Black Lady gets at least five one-liners about how complacent the white man is under Nazi rule, and one who's just there for a paycheck and bloats the script with filler. Unfortunately, the amount each one got to write is around 20/50/30, respectively.
There are moments when The New Colossus absolutely sings, where gameplay and storytelling mix to forge unforgettable encounters, but these grow more sparse and more underwhelming as the game goes on. More and more, it feels like the gameplay is taking a back seat to the cutscenes, the poor dialogue, the obsession with proving that Nazis are literally an army of Satans, and it starts to fall apart. By the end, I was thankful that the credits were rolling, only for the actual credits theme to be one of the most bizzare tonal disconnects I've seen in a long while, and I think that encapsulates The New Colossus perfectly.
This isn't why I don't recommend the game; the PC port is a ♥♥♥♥ing roulette wheel, with it often crashing or swapping the skybox with ground textures out of nowhere, only for it to run perfectly fine some other times without a single setting being changed. After the pitch-perfect polish of The New Order, this feels like a slap to the face.

I haven't played much of this game yet, but from what I have seen, I'm impressed.  I've played diffrent RPG and crafting games before and quite frankly I'm not easily impressed.  (This is after all the only review I have ever written for a game or intend to write.)  I will therefore lay out what will most likely be a rather long dissertation on a deserving game in blocks that can be digested at will in this format:
Things I didn't like (short list and always take the bad news first)
Things I liked (much longer list)
Things I would like to see integrated.  (Based on researching the game wiki and the discussions I've seen on the game's direction.)
Things I didn't like:
Not much.  Most of these have been brought up by other people, please accept this as my own take and as purely constructive criticism.
Game Speed: I use a fairly good computer, but this is the first game I've had serious latency and fps issues with.  I read up on the game and how to mitigate some of this but it is still somewhat of a system resource hog.  I've read other articles where this was brought up and I also read that this is something that may be improving as the game is refined.  It is my sincere hope that this is the case because it was the only thing the prevented me from becoming addicted and having several times more hours devoted to this game than what I have.
Animal AI: Likewise something that was brought up in different review and I agree.  In my case I kept looking around for the goats I could hear that kept getting worse and found a ditch close to my base camp where they kept falling in and the number of them kept growing.  I assume this had something to do with spawn behavior, but for now I just promised myself to return later to cash in on easily obtained goat meat as necessary.
Things I liked:
Two size blocks:  I believe this is an improvement over Minecraft.  Don't get me wrong, I love Minecraft for what it is, but this strikes me as the next logical advancement.  More complex shapes, better environment texture, all of this benefits from a larger number of building blocks available.  I have seen the type of complex mechanisms offered by games like Landmark, and I believe that this is overly involved.  A good balance similar to what is seen in Space Engineers is more desirable to me.  Possible areas for improvement would include slanted blocks so a roof can have an honest slope instead of a stair step effect.  I'm working on a thatch roof hut so it would look better that way.
Crafting Component and Crafting Surface Interface:  I will admit that at first I found this to be a bit cumbersome as I was first learning the game.  Admittedly I jumped straight in without doing that much research or watching many videos.  After I got used to it though I quickly fell in love with the quasi-realism.  The system lends itself well to using the same components in different recipes based on what work surface is being used or what tool you are holding.  It can be frustrating, but in the long run rewarding.  I could almost see a realistic NPC trainer scenario where a player coul learn a recipe by watching an NPC or other player laying out the components on the correct surface and equipping the appropriate tool.
Item Placement:  I have played Skyrim and one of the most frustrating parts of that game was the item placement mode that didn't give you much control over the items your were placing.  This game has definitely improved in that function.  Instead of containers that give you a UI panel to add and remove from similar to an inventory screen, I found myself actually making "real world" storage solutions.  My hut had wooden beam rafters where I stored my spears, poles, etc. for easy storage and retrieval.  My garden had a "compost heap" next to it where extra leaves, seeds, and other unused items went.  I am anxious to experiment with handles that I might be able to create a rack down the wall for my spears.
Visual Appearance:  This game is a promising blend of something like Skyrim and Minecraft,  The graphics are beautiful and I can't wait to explore other biomes just as soon as I'm certain I won't get lost.  The realism of the gaming experience because of the graphics combined with real life issues like getting lost in the wild give the game a very high immersion level.
Technology Level:  Where can I begin about the technology level?  Obviously, at the beginning, just like with the technology of the characters.  The opportunities for development with this game bogle the mind.  In its current state at simple bronze age technology there are a fair amount of recipes available that could be made and make a game comparable to Minecraft.  As technology levels increase, the addition of new work centers and recipes only serve to give the game additional depth.  The idea of going from Stone Age to Space Age and beyond seems enticing, but I am going to wait and see what transpires here.  It would also be similarly interesting to see higher and higher levels of magical complexity.  Rituals, better/more powerful potions, spells, and enchantments could advance with technology level as well.  This game concept has me excited.
Things I would like to see integrated:
After reading the section of the wiki on this game and seeing the yet to be introduced game elements that are still in process I wanted to be sure to add in the things that I as a gamer value and would like to see.  On the off chance that a developer might actually read this review, please take as focus group data if nothing else.
Family/Tribe Generation: One of the somewhat disappointing aspects of Skyrim and Minecraft are the social interactions with the world.  This does not necessarily entail an in depth quest and/or dialogue engine like Warcraft (Long Live CLan Arandel!) or some of the dating simulators out there.  I was looking at the 'aging' concept presented in the wiki and was hoping that we would see something that might actually allow the character to spawn progeny.  Nothing perverted mind you, but if there were a spell called 'mating ritual' you could complete near a NPC of the oppostie gender that would generate or spawn an aging offspring from toddler up to adult would be most refreshing.  The villager breeding mechanic found in Minecraft comes to mind, but the villagers leave something ot be desired in that game.  I see self generated quests as players watch a wandering monster kill a favorite offspring and then tracking the monster (or PvP player) down for revenge.
NPC generation:  I saw the article on totems that could have little podlings carrying out tasks for the character and I thought that this would be rather novel.  I like this concept and I hope it gets expanded into the ability to create a village of NPCs either through breeding (as above), conjuration, or perhaps even rescuing the people from AI Monsters.  The usefulness of these characters couold range from merely asthetic value to contributing members of a community.  I would go into more detail, but I'm running out of room in the review.
Baskets:  Stone Age containers.  I don't mind chests, but the open air basket that holds stuff would be a nice change.  As long as they are stationary and don't fly everywhere like they do in Skyrim.
Clothing:  The most customizable part of a character.  The Sims makes a fortune off of people that go onto their online store looking for new outfits for their Sims.  I think that level of variety is a bit overblown, but when playing Warcarft and all the max level characters look the same it gets kind of old.  There are several color dye possibilities with the mushrooms so a simple color shift might be enough.  I simply think that more than just leather armor should be capable of being dyed and the clothing options should change with technology level.
More work stations.  Leatherworking, tailoring, jewelry, etc.  The more the merrier.  Crap out of room.  Later!

Just to start out, I HATE playing with WADS controls, but I think I may be warming up to it with this game. Wholy sheet this game is mo-effin bad ace! I kept saying to myself "just one more level." Now, 3 hours later, my eyes hurt & I have to wait until tomorrow to play more. So far, I believe this is my favorite find on Steam! I'm super excited to see where this goes, then I get to play part 2 & 3! I can't believe a game this good was so cheap. My eyes are bleeding… but I beat the game!!! This was an amazing experience of a game. Can't wait to try #2, but I want to dominate the rest of this one & hopefully beat it on the hardest difficulty. AMAZING GAME!!! Also, totally got used to the WADS controls :)

Bought on sale and with that in mind, I recommend it for fans of classic point and click adventuring. Somewhat short (I'd say less than 10 hours on a decent "check everything" playthrough), but well-written and entertaining most of the way through. Easy and logical puzzles, so none of that "put the frog in the mouth of your younger self on a park bench" a'la the first Discworld game. There's no punishment for trying out the wrong things (if something goes wrong, you'll be right back to "just before making a wrong decision"), but the occasional saving is recommended as some parts present different solutions with slightly different outcome for the storyline.
Sure, there's some clunky animations and the occasional audio mishap, but nothing that detracts from neither gameplay nor atmosphere. If such things matter deeply to you, there's always the first Zork game to keep you up at night.
Replay value is limited, but on the whole, I enjoyed the ride while it lasted.

Normally I didn't use to gravitate towards these games, but this one caught my eye via a YouTube play-through. I draw and paint as a hobby, so this one is close to my heart. You manage a painter's guild during the Italian Renaissance and get to choose your guild's location plus your starting painter's name and looks at the start. Though everything is stylized and graphically simple, I like the management system. Your painters grow old and can get sick. They do die. You get to take in famous painters like da Vinci and Artemisia Gentileschi to help raise the prestige of your guild (which is needed to get richer clients). Your decorations also determine how high your prestige is, so the more expensive your decor, the better your guild will do with the local nobles. Ah, and be sure to buy things for your artists to mix paint with (which also raises their skills and the higher their skills, the better they paint, and the more their paintings are worth).
This game is highly addictive, but it is so worth it. You will waste a lot of time managing your little guild and hiring new painters. Reminder of new painters: make sure you study their stats, or else you may end up with a troublemaker who spends more time in jail than painting. Once the Renaissance ends, you can keep painting, but there are no more painters or events, so it kind of ends the joy a bit. There is little replayability on this one, but if you like management sims and get a lot of joy out of juggling tasks, you will enjoy this one a lot long after you've played through the Renaissance ten or fifteen times.

.

The list of bugs goes on.  I’ve yet to play a single session where I didn’t experience something odd.
All the bugs aside though, I have to say I’m really enjoying the game.  It’s a lot of fun when looked at for what it’s
to be.  And it’s clear the developers care and take stock in what the players say, as they’ve been diligently working to fix bugs since launch.  It still needs lots of work though, and hopefully the bug fixes continue.

Alright I have never written a review before, but I after seeing some of the negative reviews and reading some of the forum posts, I had to come and give my 2 cents.  First of all to the people complaining that Shelly isn't completely oversexualized so they can fap off while playing the game, shockingly there are many different body types that a human (yes including women) can have, and no not in any way does she look like a female face stuck on a male body, if that's what you think then you are really confused about male vs female body shapes.  She is a badass woman, nuff said.  Now on to the actual game.  There are definitely cons about this game I'm not gonna lie but I would definitely still recommend it, here's a list of my pros and cons.
Pros:
- Strong Female Lead Character
- Cheesy but awesome humor, one liners, puns, and I think most importantly sarcastic remarks about fetch quests and pushing buttons which while that is a lot of the gameplay actually helps keep it entertaining
- Very smooth and interesting gameplay
- Weapons that all feel unique and for the most part all feel powerful for different purposes (surprisingly hard to get right), and they all have fairly interesting upgrade paths.
- Good pacing for the story
- Really good music choices and fairly decent sound fx
- Aesthetics are fantastic, major props to the artists that worked on this
Cons:
- This game does have quite a number of bugs (health circle flickering and unrepresentative of your current health, voices randomly changing in volume and quality from one to the next was particularly irritating, bugged out enemies which just stood still and let you wail on them, and a few others)
- Fairly bad quest markers that often were not representative of where you actually had to go along with the map not allowing you to actually drag it around to view the full area
- In the weapon screen for upgrades you had to switch tabs just to go and select another weapon and you could not view the different upgrades you had actually gotten, along with no way to switch the secondary fire upgrade which was annoying to me because I would have to start another game to try out the different weapon abilities.
- Level design was actually really interesting, but due to how it was made running back and forth long distances for quests started becoming annoying and for anyone else less into the game would probably have found very annoying
- Quest variety definitely could've used some work, a lot of it was fetch quests, or hitting panels, I feel like the amiga separation should've been used more as it made for an interesting mechanic.
There is definitely more I could say but for the most part the game was a ton of fun and I can easily recommend, I look forward to seeing any future dlc and updates that come to this game, and this may be the first game in a long time I actually do a second playthrough of.  I am a solo game developer myself and thus know how hard making a game actually is, so I can very much appreciate the insane amount of work that went into this, don't let the bad reviews get you down developers, you guys made something really awesome!

This one leaves a lot more to be desired.
A top down shoot em up that doesn't seem to want to push past it's boundaries. I was intrigued at first with the story line and was actually really pumped to try the game out. Unfortunately, it fell quite short of my expectations. Bombshell follows your typical action lady that always has to swoop in and save the day. The catch? This lady has a mechanical blaster for an arm that can be swapped out for other weapons such as a mini-gun or a shotgun. The features of these guns may be upgraded with currency upon collecting it and defeating enemies. Besides having the ability to shoot, Bombshell also hones the ability to "rush". Meaning, pressing a bumper will make her slide and attack. Alternatively, there is a "punching" feature that resembles the sliding attack. There isn't much variance in either but they can stun enemies.
There are enemies that will actively dodge this attack with a jet pack. Enemies themselves are decent and are somewhat varied. It can start getting old after the second level as their attacks are not varied. They will simply chase you around and shoot while other enemies are poisonous and will slowly eat at your life. Jumping is a bit awkward in the game and some areas will look like you cannot reach them. Most areas are accessible but require a well timed jump. For beginning players, this will be frustrating as the jumps have to be at diagonals for it to be successful. The way they chose to go with the mapping scheme was a good decision. Fog of war is on and as the player explores, more of the map is available for view. Boss characters themselves I found to be sometimes unresponsive. Although they were bigger in size, they were not at all more intimidating. Some stood there just letting me shoot at them from a distance. There are consumables you can pick up along your journey. You will definitely need health packs to keep your player going. If you die no big deal. Simply respawn but lose a little cash.
The graphics themselves are okay and can be boosted to maximize the performance of your computer. Still though, nothing exceptionally amazing to catch the eye. The game will give you a small indication on the ground as to where your pointing your gun. It will auto-lock to some enemies in order to assist you. Sounds are decent but do not go over the top. Blasting sounds will get annoying whereas the dialogue from Bombshell is alright at best.
Overall, would not recommend for it's full price. I would recommend on a steep sale but not at all for the full price. The game starts getting old after the second level. Sad as it seems there could have been a lot more destruction added to the game. Just wasn't there.
RATING : 6.25/10

One of, if not the most, disappointing games of 2017.
The New Colossus starts out incredibly strong, with a killer opening level where you're rolling around on a wheelchair, shooting Nazis down staircases and up conveyor belts. It feels just like a continuation of The New Order, and that's a great thing. There's a stronger emphasis on cutscenes and storytelling, but this first level handles it extremely well, and I was absolutely gripped.
Then, the rest of the game happens.
There's a level where you're on the prowl in a radioactive wasteland, somewhat similar to Fallout 3, and your health's constantly decreasing; you jump from Nazi to Nazi to survive, scavenging armor and health packs on the way, and witnessing bodies of hundreds of irradiated civilians is an extremely somber experience. It motivates you to fight, to rebel, which is the overarching them of the game. Then you meet a sassy black lady who outmanuevers you, comments on how "only the Blacks have been fighting the Nazis," whips out her baby and starts breastfeeding it while giving a debriefing, mocks you and all your crew, and takes up a cabin of one of your dead allies, all within *five minutes* of her introduction.
It's a bit of a tonal shift.
The rest of the game suffers from this issue. It feels like the script was written by three different people: one who really wanted to push the envelope as far as story in a FPS is handled, who understood the characters of The New Order and wanted to explore *why* they fight and *what* they're fighting for, one who's there to make sure the story appeals to people who feel bitter about Trump, who does their damndest to make sure that for every sincerely touching moment, Sassy Black Lady gets at least five one-liners about how complacent the white man is under Nazi rule, and one who's just there for a paycheck and bloats the script with filler. Unfortunately, the amount each one got to write is around 20/50/30, respectively.
There are moments when The New Colossus absolutely sings, where gameplay and storytelling mix to forge unforgettable encounters, but these grow more sparse and more underwhelming as the game goes on. More and more, it feels like the gameplay is taking a back seat to the cutscenes, the poor dialogue, the obsession with proving that Nazis are literally an army of Satans, and it starts to fall apart. By the end, I was thankful that the credits were rolling, only for the actual credits theme to be one of the most bizzare tonal disconnects I've seen in a long while, and I think that encapsulates The New Colossus perfectly.
This isn't why I don't recommend the game; the PC port is a ♥♥♥♥ing roulette wheel, with it often crashing or swapping the skybox with ground textures out of nowhere, only for it to run perfectly fine some other times without a single setting being changed. After the pitch-perfect polish of The New Order, this feels like a slap to the face.
I don't know what went wrong with this game, I had every confidence in the developer to meet and exceed the merit its predecessor earned, but they fell flat in so many ways. Your money would be far better spent elsewhere.

I love this game. The gameplay is still mostly as fun as the first. The story starts off very strong. It immediately tackles issues of racism and domestic abuse during BJ's childhood and provides a decent amount of backstory for BJ and how his current state of mind is affecting his will to go on. Unfortunately, that momentum isn't maintained throughout the second half of the game. The game's tone shifts to something much more light-hearted and even more over-the-top, mostly disregarding the dark themes from the first half. It's also a few missions too short. The ending seems somewhat rushed and the ultimate goal is never really achieved. It's a shame considering Machine Games has said they didn't want to include a multiplayer because it would dilute the story. In this case, the story suffered even without multiplayer.
The gameplay hasn't changed much from The New Order or Old Blood. It's more of the same. That's not necessarily a bad thing but there are weapons you will almost never use because you have weapons that are far more effective and the ammo drops for those weapons are incredibly frequent.
If I could give the game a neutral rating, I would. However, there is still fun to be had here. Is it better than New Order and Old Blood? That's a hard sell for all the things listed above. Is it still worth picking up? Yes

Simply outstanding.
Senua's Sacrifice portrays mental illness in a disturbing, exhilarating, and (by all appearances) authentic way.  The use of binaural audio in the game is ingenious, and is integral to delivering such an impressive depiction of psychosis.  The game features stunning visuals, impactful audio, and spot-on motion capture of the main character.  All of these things come together to create a truly memorable experience.
This is absolutely worth your time and money.  I can't wait to see what Ninja Theory does next.

I followed development of Hellblade: Senua's Sacrifice for nearly two years, and must say I am very pleased with the end result.
The visual and audial style is breathtaking, and forcefully pulls you into Senua's world to great effect. The game is gorgeous and ran at a solid 80fps at 3440x1440 on my GTX 1080ti. There are a few visual bugs at ultrawide resolutions, mostly just on-screen peripheral texture/object pop-ins/outs, but nothing egregious.
Ninja Theory did an amazing job of blending the interactive game with the story interludes--they do a great job of minimizing the jarring, immersion-breaking sense you get in other games when play-time-ends-now-watch-this-cutscene-type events occur. The transitions in Hellblade are nearly seamless and I'd say they add to the experience.
Speaking of the experience: the story is amazing. I can't say this enough. I won't critique it further, you'll just have to play the game. The voice acting is top notch, genuine, and it all comes together beautifully with a wonderfully imagined game world.
The combat is a bit one-dimensional on the surface, and many players will get through the game hacking and slashing. But there is enough nuance in the combat system for a player to really leverage the attack types/combos to absolutely wreck enemies and make the game interesting. It's just too bad this isn't really required and that you _could_ simply spam the light attack all through the game (including boss fights) and make it through. I found after a while I was making the combat more interesting myself by exploring different moves--which I had to do via the Key Bindings menu as there isn't any guidance in-game.
Overall, Hellblade: Senua's Sacrifice is an excellent game, though I wish it were longer (I finished the game in 7 hours--including finding all lore stones). I was happy to support such a well crafted game at the full $29.99 at the time of release. I have put more time into cheaper games before and have come away soured... not this time!

First Impressions:
While I've played countless open-world survival sandbox games, "TUG" looked too pretty to ignore, reminding me a little bit of "Creativerse".  At first glance, I thought I'd be thrust into a caveman-esque survival fest...it turns out I was partially right.  In this case, you're actually a Seedling: "a race of humanoid beings with special crystals on their hands enabling them to interface with the strange energies and ancient secrets in the world around them".  Like a caveman (or woman), you'll start with only the basic of tools and work your way up.  While there is PVP (currently under construction), folks will be happy to learn that you can play single player in either "survival" or "creative" modes, just like in "Minecraft".  This is truly one survival sandbox game to watch out for!

Skullgirls is one of my favourite fighting games.
Skullgirls is similar in playstyle to Marvel vs Capcom 2, but has the benefit of a extra decades worth of lessons and tech improvements.
Each side can choose to fight a battle with single characters, or teams of two or three, the health and damage of the team members is scaled so that larger teams are not given an unfair advantage.
Moves are performed in typically street fighter fashion, with a six button, light medium, heavy punch/kick layout and quarter circles and charges for special moves.
The characters are uniquie and well balanced, the moves are fluid, the animation are smooth and the whole game feels incredibly polished.
The game also features a survival mode and bonus content to unlock in the form of concept art
If you have the slightest interest in arcade fighting games Skullgirls is a must buy

Really, really good game, but unfortunately too short. It took me around 5 hours to (from the very beginning) get literally everything - 8 rooms filled with best prestige items with maxed walls, roofs, floors, wallpapers, 9 level 100 painters (each in different style, excluding 4 duplicates [game has 5 styles available only]), few thousand spare cash and around 500 prestige. I am still recommending the game becuase generally, it is really enjoyable, but yet... too short boys, too short.

A cute little game but lacks depth for replayability. I'd like to see it move at a slightly slower pace over a shorter time period, some more personality in the painters, and some higher stakes for the decisions you make. Once you learn the mechanics it's very easy to have a stable of 4-5 painters at 100 skill (and a full back-burner of apprentices to fill the ranks) churning through everything that comes their way, and money ceases to be a problem. The random events don't add much challenge or offer any interesting choices, and I never saw much reason to take on grand works, since you don't lose prestige for turning them down. Here are some things I think could turn this into a great game:
- Slow the pace a bit
- Make great works higher stakes (lose prestige when you turn them down, but gain a lot when you complete them)
- More interactivity between painters (rivalries or conflicting personalities?)
- Make events more interesting (opportunity to gain lots of prestige / money at great risk, rival houses trying to poach your painters, painting in a certain style becomes ridiculously lucrative or punishing, etc.)
- Greater quantity and more diverse items
- Copies of prestige items should grant diminishing returns (beacuse a house chock-a-block with statues looks silly)

So this is a mixed review. I'm giving it a positive as I really don't think it deserves all the negative reviews it's had.
I played the game when it first came out and really enjoyed it. I liked the openness and I liked the exploration and the peace.
I've eventually got round to buying the game for myself as I saw there had been a "huge update". I'm not sure if it's this update or if it's from a previous one but the peace has been shattered. I've started 3 games in the last 2 days and died aobut 7 times. In all cases the starting planets are ridiculously sparse and there is always some element either with rads, toxins or temperature that means you can't go outside for long. In the last game a bunch of angry sentinel drones just turned up for no reason and killed me.
....to cut a long story short (too late) they seem to have made things a lot harder... but as the few people like myself who enjoyed this game did so for the calm exploration I'm not sure why.
There's definitly more flora and fauna now and i like that you can indeed start the game again instead if you really mess up. I'm just hoping they calm things down as it's a steap learning curve. You aren't really given enough of a tutorial to teach you about your scanner and visor at the beginning, and it woud be nice if the crash sites were a bit more varied as they all seem to contain the same objects in exactly the same realtive places.
I think folks should try the game out before they buy it cos either they'll love it or hate it. A better option might be The Long Dark as it has a similar feel but much more purposeful story and much more complex survival details.

I brought this game with my own money and have only play a couple of hours of the game so far. My Rig is a 750ti with an AMDFX6300 and 8GB DDR3 memory.
The game has performance issues. I slightly exceed the minium requirement, and I should reasonably be getting 60fps at medium settings at 1080p.  However even dropping the graphics to their lowest setting and dropping the resolution didn't seem to help performance at all.  I find this odd considering that the game is using UE3, and other UE3 games like Killing Floor 2 run just fine.  Even Battlefield 4 runs just fine at maxium settings.  Hopefully a patch can address this because its crippling my enjoyment of the game.
Another thing I need to address is the cutscenes have this bug where all the audio is replaced by static / white noise and I can't hear any of the dialouge.  Not sure if this ties in with the performance issues but its something worth mentioning.
I have to say the the game has a pretty decent options menu.  Pretty much everything you'd want in an options menu, even has seprate audio sliders.
Despite the perofmance issues I've been having the gameplay is really enjoyable. It doesn't feel like a Diablo clone, it feels like a Shooter. Which is a good thing, because the game is more of a shooter than an RPG.
Bombshell doesn't really speak all that much.  I honesly didn;t find her dialouge to be that funny, however the voice acting is top notch and Bombshell is propbably one of the sexiest female video game characters I've ever seen.  The story overall is more like a good old game from the Duke Nukem Era.
The visuals are pretty decent, however again my perofrmance was crippled so I couldn't enjoy them.
Overall the game is worth buying, but be aware of the performance issues if your not running the latest and greatest of systems.
Another thing I want to point out is LOWER YOUR EXPECTATIONS! This game isn't "Diablo in Space" and it isn't trying to be that.  If thats you want then this game won't cut it for you.
However for everyone else, I'd say its worth the purchase.

Bugs and glitches (and some collision issues, and the 70-odd times I died by falling through a small hole in the ground I didn't see), I absolutely loved the game!
The controls were smooth and easy, interaction with the environment was great, weapons were badass, enemies were varied enough to keep me interested and the lame 1-liners that I absolutely love (no kidding, I love lame jokes and 1-liners, they make me moist). It was exactly like I'd expect from a Duke Nukem game, but it wasn't, it was it's own little masterpiece.
Bombshell shall be a video game name I'll hold dearly for years to come. :)

I have always wanted a point and click/puzzle/adventure game where the aim is to escape a prison. So I had no doubt in my mind I wanted to get this game. All I can say after completing the game is that it's very underwhelming in terms of story and gameplay. I'll start with the story. It tries to be original and does it well on christine's side of the story, but for Joe's side of the story it's very cliche in a lot of areas. I liked a lot of the characters apart from the one that matters which is Joe, this is simply because they did a terrible job setting up a backstory for him and Christine. I like Christine's character though because she has a personality, but on the other hand Joe is such a boring, shallow and run of the mill character. As for the side characters like Viv, Sutter and Bernadette, they seem like good characters and an opportunity wasted in my opinion to expand on their backround. Mickey is a relatively interesting villain but once again has a very limited backstory.
As for the gameplay, the gameplay can get a bit repetetive as you will find yourself going back and forwards between different location's in the city of San Francisco. For a "puzzle" game the "puzzles" for the most part are extremely easy, like 90% of them are easy for one simple reason. Most of the time a character gives you a puzzle to solve they pretty much give you the solution in the dialogue options or in visual form. For instance there is a part where you have to get Mickey out of his office but it's clear that all you have to do is pretend you have a desease becasue his office is filled of cleaning equipment. Also his "bodyguard" says that Mickey just got done pretty much disinfecting his office for like an hour or so. As for the dialogue giveaways, when Joe is setting up his escape there are some garbage in the corner of the hallway. At this point in the game you are looking for a dummy to put in your bed, then he clearly states that you can use the garbage bag for a dummy. Why could'nt I figure that out for myself in a puzzle game. Also for a game where you are meant to escape prison as an inmate you spend most of your time as his wife on the outside. Which for me is good at least because I didn't really like playing as joe.
Last point, after 6-9 hours of gameplay you expect an good/interesting ending. You do not get that, all the endings are so boring (there are multiple endings which are not really different). The endings are so cliche and not satisfying at all.
I would reccomend this game if it's on sale or if you are a massive point and click/adventure/puzzle fan. If you are not a fan of the genre or the Alcatraz topic I would not give this game more than a borrow from a friend.
All the other points I didn't write about are down below.
+Good map design
+Alright voice acting
+Varied locations (in terms of buildings not settings)
+Servicable animations
-Achievements didn't work for me for some reason (I only got two achievements instead of the 9-12 I deserve)
-Odd character walking speed
-Way too many loading screens
-Side characters don't have backstory's which feels like a massive opportunity wasted
Thank you for reading, I hope you enjoyed and this helped you make an informed decision on whether to buy this game or not.

The game surrounds a guy named Joe who gets arrested and sent to Alcatraz for a robbery. It revolves around a point and click style of gameplay that has you clicking everywhere to look for clues. The story is pretty o-k, but nothing too amazing. You get a lot of options with most characters, and a lot of the options you choose can effect other characters in the game.
The voices and settings of the game are pretty decent, and I enjoyed them while playing. Sometimes the dialogue can be a bit extended but good thing they have a skip function when you click.
However, the reason I'm giving it a negative review is because there is a good possibility that when you're playing, the game bugs out and you're not able to complete an objective. This personally happened to me (and a few others), where in a scene when you're supposed to use an object on a character, the character instead doesn't react to the object and no matter what you do you can't progress.
In addiition to that specific bug, numerous people have also experienced bugs with achievements and other aspects of gameplay.
This may not be the case for everyone, but it was for me and a few others I have saw around. It's possible you may have a different outcome so pick this game up at a heavy discount. It could be entertaining if you don't encounter a game breaking bug.
4/10

1954 Alcatraz is a point-and-click adventure with great art style, for the most part good voice actors, and some nice music. Unfortunately, it fails to hook you as its story and characters have potential, but you only get to scratch the surface. You'd want to get to know these people and their backgrounds better to be able to get involved and interested in their stories. Even after a few hours, I still haven't got a good reason as to why I should care for the main characters. One or two humorous dialogue options and some random bad guys out to get them doesn't really make me motivated.
The main reason that I cannot recommend this game, though, is a game breaking oversight too many hours in.
Near the end, there is a part where you have to switch between the characters to make one of them bring some items for the other one. However, if you trigger an event that makes the story proceed BEFORE you've brought every item needed, you'll get stuck with the other character, unable to switch to the item bringing one since the game considers their part to be done. In other words: You won't get the items needed, you can't switch character and you can't finish the game. There is absolutely no indication that this will happen and you do not get a game over. All you can do is aimlessly wander around with your active character and do nothing at all.
Since the game doesn't tell you that you screwed up and obviously expects you to have done everything in the correct order before proceeding (which you possibly cannot know before you've made the mistake), I assume that this isn't on purpose but a bug that seemingly has been ignored by the developers; Take a look at the discussions page and you'll find more players running into the same problem a year before I did.
Even without this bug, or whatever it should be classified as, 1954 Alcatraz is definitely not worth 19,98€. The story and character writing is too uninspired and messy, the animations are a bit clunky and there are a couple too many black and/or loading screens, often interrupting the end of the scenes. If you're a huge adventure/point-and-click fan, then you might wanna give it a chance, but look for a huge discount first.

- Very detailed animation of Gay Men making out everytime you return to a particular location (you need to return there many times). I have to admit that
went and snatched the first place among my favorite Artifex Mundi games so far. I wonder why I haven't played this earlier. I knew I was getting myself a satisfactory HOG when I bought this, but I had no idea that I'll be having this grand a deal in HOG genre!
In a fictional steampunk version of 1700 Prussia, we take the role of Evangeline Glass; Dr. Ink's protégé and engineer extraordinaire. We hit the road to meet with the good doctor in Hochwald, part of Habsburg Monarchy at the time, on a letter that we receive from him earlier. Dr. Ink has been making a research on the alarmingly raising number of earthquakes that were dominating the area. He claims that he has proof that a corruption in local authority is responsible: General Engineer is abusing a dangerous machine to create these earthquakes and he should be stopped at once!
At this point, we all know what kind of game that we should be expecting from Artifex Mundi: beautiful artwork, genuine animations, charming setting, and a curious story. Above all our common expectations,
covers a narration and a period so dark, yet envelops it with fair music and an atmosphere straight out of fables. The marriage of Austrian culture with Enlightenment science gives birth to this amazing game. As a personal favorite, I couldn't avoid to mention the puzzle of Saints during the bonus chapter, which is a direct example of this marriage. Did I mention the artwork? I know I'm trying my chance, but even the achievements interface itself is an artwork, made of stain glass!
Gameplay is ordinary, yet the adventure elements of assembling machines are fairly imaginative. There aren't many HOG scenes, rather FROG - fragmented object game - scenes dominating this particular game. There is little to no backtracking, and a full functioning map. Puzzles are the kind that we are used to by now. As a change, in this particular adventure, we have the luxury of utilizing Matthew, a mechanical crow that we send out to gather items out of our reach, which spices the gameplay a bit up. We are also entitled to enjoy a bonus chapter at the end, to experience Dr. Ink's short adventure before Evangeline's arrival. The game is pretty short, being 5 hours or so with the bonus chapter.
Once I've completed the bonus chapter, I wholeheartedly wished there would be a series of Clockwork Tales games. I usually prefer downright fantasy or at least mythological elements in storylines, but
is an elegant exception that I'll let myself be enthusiastic about. As a side note, I'm in love with the steam machine crow named Matthew!

As you would expect from any AM HOG, this is a fairly well polished game (for the genre), which is easy to play and has a decent storyline, in this case set in a steampunk fantasy world. While the game isn't particularly long, it is otherwise hard to criticize - the story moves along reasonably well, the gameplay is solid throughout - the HOG scenes are good, the point and click and puzzles all flow fairly well and make sense.
Probably the main area it could have been improved would have been better characterization or development of the three main characters, you barely interact with the main bad guy, and you only talk to your mentor a couple of times, so most of the story is developed through the protagonist narrating what is happening. Despite that, this is one of the better HOG games around, so it is an easy one to recommend for those that like this type of game.

People often forget, when talking about the Assassins Creed series, the ambitious story and theme that the first game attempted to sell to a new fan base. This first instalment in the series is often criticised for its repetitive missions and clunky fighting mechanics, fair criticism as well, but what people have missed is that as the series has improved in terms of game play and setting, the intellectual discussion on power and choice has taken a back seat. Gone are the multifaceted antagonists and questionable ethics of the first game. If you want to play a game that asks you whether might makes right and whether murdering somebody is ever a good deed, that questions your moral assumptions, I think you should play this game to the end.

I've made it about 70% of the way through the game as of now, and man....this is epic. I'll keep it simple.
Verdict: 9/10. Should be the FIRST game you pick up when there's a sale, or if you can't wait, 30$ isn't that bad. But you could probably find slightly better. On sale, though, BUY BUY BUY.
Pros:
- INCREDIBLE art direction.
- Soundtrack is out of this world good. Like, for real, it's up there with my favorite soundtracks. Very future-esque feel.
- Though the main character sometimes sounds like she's out of some modern shakespeare novel, there are moments where this story truly shines as a serious masterpiece.
- Neo-Paris is jaw-dropping.
- Graphics are very, very good. (Maybe it's just me - but Neo-Paris in the rain is so, sooooo cool.)
- Memory Remixing is a very cool element - didn't think i'd like it, but seeing the cause vs. effect in them is cool.
- Only 70% of the way through the story at about 10 hours, and i'm usually a fast-ish player.
Cons:
- Clunky controls. Not SUPER clunky, but enough to say "Well, this is slightly annoying."
- NO STEALTH! :(
- Fighting style does get repetitive after awhile - I did find myself having to take a break because of it, unfortunatly.
- Very "on-rails" - there's not really much exploration, except for what they show you. I wish the game would let you explore ALL of Neo Paris. Now that would be absolutely incredible and probably make it my favorite game of all time.
- Quicktime events don't serve boss fights justice.
- Encountered 1-2 bugs during gameplay, and had to restart from a checkpoint. Good news is, you lose about 20 seconds most of the time. Not a big deal, but still.
- Seems like there was a lot of potential in this game that was missing, possibly from a rushed game schedule? Capcom...
TL:DR: Great game with a lot of potential possibly ruined by bad control design along with lack of exploration.

Trine is more "good idea" than good game. I don't think I ever finished it, and I didn't even care enough to do so before playing Trine 2. The story is uninteresting, the characters are one-note, and the gameplay is pretty simple. You run and jump around in glowy locations that are sometimes attractive. If you're the warrior, you can block attacks with a shield and kill enemies with a weapon. If you're the wizard, you can create boxes and platforms to assist with maneuvering the terrain. If you're the assassin, you can kill with a bow and arrow, and swing from a grappling hook. Like I said, it's a good idea, but playing this by myself, I just could not get into the game and didn't really like it.
The sequel, however, is more of the same, with a few new features, it has lovely backgrounds, and it's
. Having other players in a world that would otherwise make me sleepy due to a lack of narrative drive or exciting gameplay meant I could chat with my friends while we tried to solve puzzles and such together. You don't need to play Trine to enjoy Trine 2, and given how similar their gameplay is and the plot's simplicity and near-non-existence, you're better off picking up Trine 2 and playing it with friends. Grab that sucker on sale, get some folks on Steam chat with mics who you like to discuss things with, and have a good time.

Painters Guild is a 2d management base building experience with an artistic flair. The options menu is very simplistic, with only the option of full screen or windows mode.  This game walks a fine line in it's methodology of progression. It is entertaining to a point, but once you hit that plateau then it becomes repetitive nonsense with heavy taxation on your resources. If this game is on sale, I would recommend it, but because this game has no true feeling of becoming a legendary artist, only the continuous climb and burden of ownership, management or taxation on your character, there is no feeling of relief or pride in your accomplishment.

It is a time management game, where you accept contracts to create paintings, and have to manage rest for your character, keeping your supplies stocked, and the prestige of your studio. Prestige is the means to lure in higher paying clients- improved by putting out higher quality work, and finishing contracts, as well as improving your home base. You have the capability to hire more people, who have various strengths and weaknesses.
The game is very management oriented, where you build and expand a base, utilize your hired units to ensure growth of the company, and attract higher quality clients that will pay more. In between 30-60 minutes of play, you will reach a plateau in the game, where there are is nothing else to unlock, no more variables that occur. As you build your base larger, the tasks become repetitive. It's a click and drag mentality, the same tasks over and over again.
There is an occasional special project, such as a cathedral, but I've found that the time it takes to complete this task and the numberof people it takes can be more detrimental to your business than not. Most times it's easier to focus on the painting and building aspect rather than focusing on the prestige or special projects.
As you grow larger and become more engulfed into the world, and your prestige  gets higher, you will attract customers with specific requests. This can be potentially disastrous, as it takes years for your characters to get to master status in any one style of artwork and your painters do die throughout the game. If you can't handle the continuous instream, you can end up watching everything you've worked so hard for crumble rapidly in front of you. Artistically this might fall right into the story of an artist, but gameplay wise it doesn't work, for you art does not live on.

This game is tricky. It may look easy, but it's deceptively so.
You start off with a single painter who needs to train up an apprentice. You quickly learn about the different painting styles while you try to keep your head above the water and throw painting after painting out the door.
Occasionally you get requests to help paint works of art for local buildings, which soon ask for more than just two painters.
So you take on a second apprentice, build out to accomodate them, then a third... and soon you're juggling them all trying to get their skills up, keep the paint flowing, and worry yourself sick about whether your master painter will survive long enough to see their apprentices become master painters themselves.
It's a good game, but if you're expecting a casual approach, you'll soon find you're mistaken. This game gets progressively more difficult to manage.

I remember catching word of this game a few years before it released last year, and being stoked as could be. Sean had showed all these awesome videos at a ton of different interviews. It was suppose to have an endless universe of planets to explore, each unique and different in their own way. He showed space battles, combating freighters and other ships in some epic space battle footage, and then went on to mention that we'd be able to play with our friends but the chances of encountering said friends would be astronomically low due to their procedual generation algorithm.
Well August 9th came and all we found were a bunch of planets and a bunch of creatures on them that sure were procedually generated, but their generator didn't have more than 6 different ways to throw an eyeball in some random place, and the planets were basically all of the same, without any being visually appealing whatsoever. Then, of course, it turns out that being able to encounter others was a load of rubbish as they hadn't even created character models. Sean Murray overestimated their algorithm.
Fast Forward a year and now they have the 1.3 Update. Still no true multiplayer, you just see orbs when you encounter others, which I guess is a step up from seeing nothing, but what's the point of the orb? You can't do anything together still so it's pointless. They added "variety" to the planets, which is nice, but again, you've had the game out for over a year and this was suppose to be in the original release. Space Battles are still meh and nothing near as epic as the video Sean showed off a few years ago.
This game is interesting if you have nothing better to do I guess, but next to that, you're just playing it for the sake of trying to find some kind of self gratification. There is no building bases with friends, or any activity to be done with friends beyond communicating in game, I can do that in discord or Teamspeak though.
We all paid $60 for an Early Access game that now since they've updated it "more" in the direction that the game was SUPPOSED to be in at launch, it's 50% off, closer to what the game is actually worth, but I still don't think this one is worth more than $15. There are people that love it, and so be it, it's not my time or place to judge them for it, but I highly recommend looking elsewhere because there is absolutley NOTHING Hello Games can do to make up for the sheer amount of lies they prsented us with prior to launch.

Bombshell is the latest action game from Interceptor and 3D Realms where you play as Shelly 'Bombshell' Harrison, a colonel who lost her arm and her comrades in an explosion created by the professor Jadus Heskel but thanks to the military she is now sporting a cybernetic arm made of unknown material  that can transform into muliple heavy weapons and with it she will take her revenge on the mad professor.
Bombshell is a game that has a slight more in depth system in place than what you would typically find in a twin stick shooter. With basic RPG mechanics like leveling up to earn skill points as well as weapon upgrading as long as you have the cash and are of the right character level. It's hard not to make comparisons to this and an ARPG like Diablo or Torchlight as it's all set in an isometric view and in giant levels that have you exploring to uncover dark areas of the map to find quest items. However it doesn't go far enough with that genre as there are no loot drops other than cash that can you use to upgrade your weapons.
The actual game play is good thanks to the weapons. Each weapon can be upgraded to become much more powerful as well as giving the player the option to go upgrade it down one of two paths for wildly different alt fire attacks. The default Ion Maiden with ulimited ammo can be upgraded to also have a rail gun alt fire if you choose or the shotgun that can also fire explosive shells. Action can be hectic as you lob a homing grendade that can explode into a cluster at a group of enemies and watch their explosive deaths unfold.
As you level up you dump 2 skill points into either your Health, Armor  or Energy or into any one of the four powers. Those powers are mega punch, dodge, energy shield or sword that can be once activated wil consume energy. I personally found the energy shield to be quite effective as it dealt damage to enemies that came into contact with it. You can also earn one skill point by occasionally completing a quest although some of these quests items are deviously hidden in these large maps that I missed quite a few when actively looking for them.
The game does boast some striking visuals all thanks to the Unreal Engine and with no pop ins to speak of I'm quite pleased with how it looks. The environments looks great, from the sandy ruins of Kyrron to the frozen lakes of Zeroth and the red metallic surfaces of the Planet Eater. Shelly the main protagonist also has a great character design and is a much bigger improvement over what she use to look like back when the game was first unveiled. Enemy designs are good too though a bigger variety per planet would have been welcomed.
Audio is also good with guitar solos picking up right when the action heats up and it helps fit within the tone of the game. However not all of it is good, while Shelly herself sounds good it's mainly the voices of the marines that just sound awful. also some of the heavy guitar solos can carry on longer even when there is no action and no enemies to kill though this is a rare occurrence. A positive note though is John St John voicing the anatagonist Jadus Heskel and it was good because I couldn't pick his voice out.
There are a few caveats I have with the game such as falling off the edge killing you instantly although death isn't too punishing. Aslo in my 10 hours of playing through it the game crashed on me twice. Also those levels are really big that lead to tediously running around as you find quest items and hand them back to the quest giver. For some reason you can't move around the map screen with the controller so I had to use the mouse which aslo wasn't great as you couldn't move the map too far without it snapping back to you position. Some of the one liners and execution moves can be repetitive as well but it isn't too bad.
I didn't know what to expect from this game when coming in. I thought maybe it would have too many dumb referential jokes and while there are some of those I'm actually pleased that the character Shelly isn't like Duke only spitting out one liners. Shes a hardened soldier that other marines respect and has smart things to say about certain situations and the conversations between her and her arm A.I. Amiga are good. There's a part in the story where Shelly learns a truth and her animosity towards a certain character was well handled. For me this is how she stays relevent for years to come in an era that isn't strictly attitude like the 90's where Duke was good.
With a good game length as well as a New Game Plus as you won't be able to upgrade everything on your first playthough I recommend playing this game.

I'm not the sort to prejudice games over things like their being hidden object puzzlers; and the Artifex Mundi games are by far the best examples of the genre. Nonetheless A.M. has followed the method of if it isn't broke don't fix it, meaning they reuse their puzzles with cosmetic variations from one game to another. This has the unfortunate result that if you've played one of their games you've played them all.
That's O.K. if you think of the games as more visual novels with bonus puzzle content. Granted the writing isn't amazing; but it isn't bad either. I know I've yet to play an A.M. game I could make myself stop playing before the end. That's, on average, over 3 hours in one sitting. And, most of their games include a bonus chapter that extends gameplay another hour.
They do manage to do this without unnecessarily padding game length that overstays its welcome. I know that doesn't sound like much in an industry with triple AAA titles that boast hundred of hours of gameplay. But, for cheap casual games this is an achievement.
My recommendation, because of the "if you've played one you've played them all" problem, is pare your selections down to their better games. That would be Enigmatis 2 (but not the mediocre Enigmatis: the Ghosts of Maple Creek) as a top pick, Grim Legends 1 & 2 if you liked that, and the Nightmares from the Deep trilogy if you just can't get enough of these games.
